items.body: The Prom on August 20 commemorated the centennial of Miles Davis’s birth. Davis was undoubtedly one of the greatest and most important musicians of the 20th century, but he was not a composer and not just a performer. He was a composing performer, who probably never played the same thing the same way twice. His playing is known to many people, just about everybody now, through his recordings, which were a single example of how he would have done something, and which are also very much a product of his work with arrangers, most especially Gil Evans. It is their collaboration which is known through recordings such as Miles Ahead, Sketches of Spain, and Porgy and Bess. But those recordings can’t just be recreated, nor would anybody want them to be. So the audience for this Prom heard Ambrose Akinmusire, trumpet, Sam Harris, piano, Harish Raghavan, bass, Kendrick Scott, drums, along with the BBC Concert Orchestra, conducted by Miho Hazama, all of them very very fine and wonderful musicians, evoking, through their own playing and different arrangements, which were nonetheless evocations of the famous arrangements, mostly by Gil Evans, the magical quality of Davis’s recordings, and for the most part it all succeeded wonderfully. (For this listener, for instance, the performance of My Ship came far short of the character and quality of Davis’s recording). The program for the concert had a very detailed and informative account of Davis’s life and the development of his career by Alyn Shipton. It also included a short interview with Ambrose Akinmusire about Davis’s influence on succeeding musicians and, in fact, on some of the issues discussed above. It was altogether a very enjoyable evening of music making, celebrating Davis’s creations and achievements.The bulk of the Prom two nights earlier, presented by the BBC Symphony Orchestra, conducted by Cristian Mãelaru, was occupied by the Symphony No. 10 by Shostakovich. That work was preceded, though, by Skyline, a concerto for three percussionists and timpani by Édith Canat de Chizy, which was a BBC co-commission and which was receiving its UK premiere. The soloists were Lucy Landymore, Emma Arden, Delia Stevens, and Richard Cartidge. Skyline over its twenty minute length traces five stages from the emerging of the universe from blackness, through the dawn of the cosmos, the birth of different kinds of starts, the explosion and rhythm of pulsars, to the death of the cosmos. The four soloists were positioned around the orchestra which in fact became a sort of amplifier of their sounds and, in fact, of the argument of the work. The work was continually compelling in its sounds and riveting in its progress. Canat de Chizy was a composers I knew nothing about before this encounter and one who I will look out for going forward. Probably due to the very oppressive cultural climate of the last years of Stalin’s rule in Russia, Shostakovich wrote, or at least, released very few major works during that time. The Tenth Symphony appeared a few months after Stalin’s death, and it was taken, and is probably still taken, as a commentary on that situation. The very abrasive scherzo, the second movement was apparently intended as a portrait of Stalin. This performance presented the work to its fullest advantage. The advertising and presentation of this concert, which mentioned the Shostakovich only and the Canat de Chizy not at all, is an example of how the BBC is currently presenting these concerts in general. In this case, one might have assumed that the Shostakovich was the only piece on the concert, and one would have had to dig deep, or at least deeper, to find that there was another piece on the concert, and that it was by a living composer and had been commissioned by the BBC. The inclusion of newer pieces used to be celebrated; now it’s more or less hidden. The tactic seems pretty clear. One wonders if this particular approach to things really produces a larger audience, which is presumably the goal. In a similar manner, the Prom of the 21st of August, presented by The BBC Philharmonic, conducted by Anja Bihlmaier, with soloists tenor Clay Hiley and mezzo soprano Jamie Barton, only promoted the final work on the concert, Das Lied von der Erde by Mahler, without mentioning the pieces on the first half of the concert, the Haydn Farewell Symphony (No. 45, in f sharp minor) and Mosaic by Bushra El-Turk. El-Turk is a British composer of Lebanese descent whose work has been very much involved with the integration of eastern and western musical elements. Mosaic, lasting 8 minutes, which was receiving its first performance at the Proms, was commissioned by the Manchester Camerata for a season which explored the question of cross-pollination of ideas between cultures. It’s compelling shape is one of increasing activity and intensity from the beginning to a climactic point where the bottom falls out of things and there is a very quiet music which evokes Byzantine chant which concludes the piece after a very brief reminiscence of the previous activity. It was a fine beginning to a concert of equally compelling pieces, all of them masterfully performed. The post BBC Proms Miles Davis, Canat de Chizy, El-Turk, Shostakovich appeared first on Sequenza21.
items._cn_summary: 文章记录BBC逍遥音乐节两场音乐会。首场为纪念Miles Davis百年诞辰，Ambrose Akinmusire小号领衔四重奏与BBC音乐会管弦乐团合作，以新编曲重释Gil Evans的经典编配，氛围再现Davis录音的神韵但未完全复制原作。其次介绍Édith Canat de Chizy的协奏曲《Skyline》，由四位打击乐独奏与管弦乐队呈现，描绘宇宙从诞生到消亡的五阶段历程，乐队充当声音放大器，音色引人入胜。最后论及肖斯塔科维奇第十交响曲，因斯大林时期压抑文化环境而作品产出受限。整体评述横跨爵士重新演绎、当代委约新作及二十世纪交响经典。

items.body: On A Violent Power and Bontempi Pop 3, Danz CM treats synthesizers less like collector’s trophies than working machinery, using vintage hardware to build pop that moves, mutates, and occasionally grins at its own oscillations. The equipment may be old, but the decisions feel immediate: basslines snap into position, keyboards dart through the margins, and every unusual texture seems enlisted because it can push the song somewhere useful. A Violent Power is the straighter shot. Constructed entirely from analogue synths, it runs on a rigid new-wave pulse that suggests Kraftwerk’s immaculate engineering after somebody slipped a little danger into the control room. Berlin and Ladytron provide useful coordinates, particularly in the marriage of cool surfaces and emotional excess, yet Danz gives the track enough pressure to keep the references from swallowing it. The song concerns surrendering to an overpowering emotion, and the arrangement keeps tightening around that idea, adding momentum until submission starts sounding suspiciously pleasurable. Synth lines rise, retreat, and lock together with the tidy aggression of machinery designed for dancing. Then Bontempi Pop 3 wanders into stranger territory and steals the double single. Its breakbeat shuffles with trip-hop weight while an Italian Bontempi toy organ squeaks, chirps, and zips across the track as though somebody left a children’s keyboard unsupervised in an experimental studio. Broadcast supplies some of its crooked sweetness, while the toy-box melodies carry the idyllic whimsy of Danish synth band Moral, and the repetition has Stereolab’s playful momentum. Just this side of psychedelia, the arrangement keeps producing small surprises without turning into a crowded demonstration of gear. The subject is time: specifically, the desire to escape its disappearing act by occupying the present more completely. That could easily become heavy-handed philosophy, but Danz wisely gives the idea movement rather than solemnity. The beat keeps walking forward while those peculiar keyboards seem determined to distract the clock. Together, the singles reveal a musician with enough technical command to know that technical command is boring when displayed for its own sake. Live guitars, acoustic drums, motorik rhythms, layered vocals, and banks of synthesizers enter according to function rather than prestige, allowing touches of Nation of Language, Chromatics, Ladytron, Stereolab, and Broadcast to flash past without turning the songs into record-collection bookkeeping. A Violent Power provides the immediate hook, but Bontempi Pop 3 supplies the mischief. One is streamlined and commanding; the other keeps poking holes in its own geometry. Listen to A Violent Power/Bontempi Pop 3 below or via the streaming service of your choice here: Originally from New York’s Catskill Mountains and now based in Los Angeles, Danz CM first built an audience during the 2010s as Computer Magic, operating with a staunch DIY approach that eventually produced records including 2015’s Davos and led to considerable success in Japan, where her music appeared in campaigns for Panasonic and Kewpie Mayo. After retiring the Computer Magic name, she moved further into composition and instrumental arrangement, scoring independent films including While Mortals Sleep and Gary Hustwit’s The Map. During the pandemic she also founded Synth History, the print publication devoted to synthesizers, electronic music, and the people behind them, while continuing to write, produce, mix, art-direct, and release music through her own Channel 9 Records. Recent releases have moved from the ambient abstractions of MYTHS to the krautrock excursions of 2025’s LÄRM!, alongside tours supporting LCD Soundsystem and Ladytron. items._cn_summary: 这张双单曲展示了复古合成器在流行框架中的灵活运用。《A Violent Power》以全模拟合成器构建新律动脉冲，旋律线在Kraftwerk式的精密工程与暗藏危险的张力间游走，编曲围绕情绪屈服的主题不断收紧节奏。《Bontempi Pop 3》则走向怪诞方向，将碎拍节拍与意大利Bontempi玩具风琴结合，玩具旋律穿梭于实验音色之间，主题关于逃离时间的流逝感。两首作品均体现技术服务于功能的理念，乐器与合成器依据歌曲需要进入，避免炫耀式堆砌。引用坐标涵盖Ladytron、Broadcast、Stereolab、Nation of Language等乐队，融合冷调表面与情绪张力，但整体仍偏向合成器流行的可听性范畴。

items.body: I need to know And maybe we can talk about And maybe we can try to solve it Take me by the hand and take me away Heartbreak rarely proceeds with literary dignity. People sulk, contradict themselves, make declarations they abandon ten minutes later, and discover that wounded pride is a lousy substitute for company. The same voice that insists, “I don’t need you,” can soon confess, “I miss you.” French Police build their new double single, Super Over Drive / Silver, around that reversal, tracing the distance between defensive solitude and the admission that another person is still wanted. The release follows July’s Reptile / Japan, the double single that opened the Chicago trio’s new chapter with Interscope Records. On Reptile, Brian Flores looked toward companionship as a possible escape from thoughts he could not quiet. Super Over Drive takes that need into more combative territory, allowing loneliness to sour into anger before Silver strips away the posture and asks whether speaking plainly might still save something. French Police have spent the better part of their existence making romantic catastrophe sound unusually well-dressed, and these paired songs carry that instinct into bigger, cleaner arrangements without disguising the embarrassment in the words. There is still enough black-clad cool here to populate three basement clubs, but Flores sounds increasingly willing to let the mask slip, giving both songs their peculiar charge. Super Over Drive runs on a bass line with the stubborn forward motion of somebody walking home at 3 a.m. because calling a cab would require admitting the night went badly. The rhythm section keeps everything locked down while Manny Herrera’s guitar rises, retreats, then slices back through the arrangement from another angle. Flores stretches his phrasing farther than usual, holding notes until the romantic detachment begins to crack. His voice carries composure and panic simultaneously, a useful combination for a song about insisting you can live without anybody while secretly hoping somebody will notice you are drowning in your own apartment. Directed by Chris Eichenseer, the accompanying video frames the band through a sepia-tinted, abstract performance that feels appropriately unstable. Bodies blur into movement, faces appear and disappear through unusual compositions, and the muted brown tones give the footage the quality of some damaged transmission dug out of an abandoned television studio. It is moody, slightly trippy, and strange in exactly the right proportions, extending the song’s sense of emotional dislocation without explaining any of it away. Watch the video for Super Over Drive below: Silver turns the temperature down, balancing spacious guitar interplay, vocal reach, and carefully controlled escalation while leaving more room around Flores’ voice. Here the problem is communication itself: caring without saying so, sensing that something has broken, and wondering whether two people can still name the damage before it becomes permanent. The song carries guilt without theatrical punishment. Its final admissions of absence and need land with the blunt force of somebody finally saying what should have been said weeks earlier. Watch the video for Silver below: Founded by Mexican-American singer, songwriter, and guitarist Brian Flores in 2018, French Police—with Herrera on lead guitar and Rolando Donjuan on bass—came out of Chicago with obvious debts to Interpol while steadily developing a romantic severity closer to the international post-punk culture surrounding Molchat Doma, Lebanon Hanover, The Chameleons, and KINO. At the very moment a major-label deal promises to enlarge their world, Super Over Drive and Silver keep French Police focused on the smaller disaster: two people sitting close enough to speak, each waiting for the other to go first. items.body: Scheitan, the gothic rock band from Luleå in northern Sweden, released a lyric video for Queen of The Lions on 28 August 2026. The band describe the track as a dark and gloomy goth ballad, and it reaches the major streaming platforms on Friday 4 September. It is the first taste of a new, as yet untitled album that the band say will follow in 2027 through The Circle Music. Queen of The Lions by Scheitan Who made ‘Queen of The Lions’ The song runs 3:50. Pierre Törnkvist wrote the lyrics, and the music is credited jointly to Törnkvist and Swedish producer Daniel Bergstrand, who also mixed the track at his Dugout Studio in Uppsala. Bergstrand’s engineering and production credits take in In Flames, Meshuggah, Soilwork, Dimmu Borgir, At The Gates and Behemoth, and he is not new to this band: he mixed Scheitan’s 2024 album “Songs For The Gothic People”. The single artwork is by ErlikWindsteel. The band play the Hellsinki Industrial Festival in Finland on 19 November 2026. The eighth edition of the festival runs from 19 to 21 November, with the opening night at On The Rocks in central Helsinki and the two following nights at Tiivistämö. Scheitan share that first bill with Agent Side Grinder and Stuka; Gothminister and Extize are among the acts on the later nights. About Scheitan Scheitan formed in Luleå, in Norrbotten in northern Sweden, in 1996, around Pierre Törnkvist and Oskar Karlsson. The band’s first three albums ran through a fast stylistic arc, from black metal into a rougher rock idiom: “Travelling in Ancient Times” appeared in 1996 on the German label Invasion Records, “Berzerk 2000” followed on the same label in 1998, and “Nemesis” came out on Century Media in 1999. All three were recorded in Luleå with engineer Göran Norman. The band then stopped. Törnkvist kept working. He plays in Helltrain, which he started with Karlsson and his younger brother Patrik Törnkvist, and in Devil’s Force. Karlsson died in 2016. Scheitan restarted in 2021 with the “Deathgoth” EP, and returned in earnest in 2023 with three singles, “Lost in Time”, “Fire at Dawn” and a cover of Billy Idol’s “White Wedding”, all pointing at gothic rock rather than the band’s 1990s output. The Greek label The Circle Music has released the two albums since. “Songs For The Gothic People” came out on 22 May 2024, preceded by the single “Believe” in January that year, and was recorded in Luleå and mixed by Bergstrand. “Wine For a Tormented Soul” followed on 19 December 2025 with eight tracks written by Törnkvist, trailed by the singles “Carry Me Home” and “Heaven Tonight”. Törnkvist discussed the band’s second run in a 2024 Side-Line interview. “Queen of The Lions” is the first release since the standalone single “A Million Days” earlier in 2026, and the first from the album planned for 2027.
items._cn_summary: 瑞典哥德摇滚乐队Scheitan来自北部的吕勒奥，2026年8月发布单曲《Queen of The Lions》的歌词视频，作为2027年新专辑的首支单曲。词作者皮埃尔·通恩奎斯特与瑞典制作人丹尼尔·贝里斯特兰德共同创作，贝里斯特兰德在乌普萨拉的Dugout Studio完成混音。贝里斯特兰德的工程与制作履历覆盖In Flames、Meshuggah、Dimmu Borgir等金属及极端金属领域，与该乐队过往作品《Songs For The Gothic People》也有合作。乐队1996年成立，早期作品从黑金属转向摇滚，后于2021年重启，回归哥德摇滚路线。希腊厂牌The Circle Music发行其近两张专辑。乐队将参加11月在芬兰举办的第八届Hellsinki Industrial Festival。

items.body: Thierry Kiranga was born in Katana, in the Democratic Republic of Congo, on the shores of Lake Kivu, and raised across the border in Bujumbura, Burundi, before civil war forced him to Italy. His new single, “Hard Times,” follows March’s “Ciao” and arrived July 17 on Roble Records. He learned to sing and to play guitar, drums and percussion under two Burundian mentors, Jean Christophe Matata and Canjo Amissi. Music ran in the family before that: his mother founded and still directs the Santa Cecilia choir, and his father sang tenor with the SOSAT choir and played violin on some of Italy’s earliest television broadcasts. Kiranga later studied Afro-Cuban jazz at Milan’s CPM conservatory, specialising in drums and percussion, and released his debut album, Asante, in the summer of 2023. “Hard Times” was recorded at Roble Factory Studio in Alghero, Sardinia, produced and mixed by Antonio Leardi and mastered by Simone Squillario. Choral harmonies sit over rhythms drawn from Kiranga’s Afro-Caribbean and European influences.The lyrics call out a broken promise: a world that claims to offer safety and prosperity while treating anyone different as a threat. Kiranga’s answer is to look to older generations for guidance, the same instinct that sent him to Matata and Amissi as a teenager and that he grew up watching in his own parents. On stage, Kiranga performs with an eight-piece band, The Backyard Embassy, drawing bass, guitar, keys, percussion, horns and backing vocals from players based across Italy, France, the US and Bulgaria. Stream “Hard Times” HERE The post Daily Discovery: Thierry – Hard Times appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items._cn_summary: Thierry Kiranga 出生于刚果民主共和国基伍湖畔，在布隆迪成长，后因内战迁居意大利。他的单曲《Hard Times》延续了非洲-加勒比节奏与欧洲和声的融合路线：合唱式人声铺设在跨文化律动之上，歌词直指当代世界的虚伪承诺——宣称安全与繁荣，却将差异视为威胁。Kiranga 的回答是回望长辈寻求指引，这与他少年时跟随两位布隆迪导师学习歌唱、吉他、鼓与打击乐的成长经历一脉相承。其父亲曾在意大利早期电视广播中演奏小提琴，母亲创立并至今主持圣塞西莉亚合唱团，家族音乐血脉深厚。Kiranga 曾在米兰音乐学院主攻非洲-古巴爵士，擅长鼓与打击乐，2023年发行首张专辑《Asante》。该曲在撒丁岛录制，由 Antonio Leardi 制作混音。现场演出搭配八人乐队，成员来自意大利、法国、美国与保加利亚，体现跨国合作格局。整体定位为独立厂牌世界音乐融合作品，与主流商业制作保持距离。

items.body: American label Florabelle will release a couple of ambient gems at the end of March. Both fit in with the promise of spring and its lighter, brighter season. The label was conceived in 2014 and calls New York its home, but these two releases, while remaining in the US, head south and west. The first, Coquina Dose, by Josh Mason, features a tight ecosystem of warm tones and microscopic particles. Influenced by the barometric pressure of a humid summer day, its pond-like ripples are pockmarked by dusty crackles and light, organic tones which hover around like dragonflies at noon. Inspired by Josh’s lifelong home of Florida, the humid climate of the Sunshine State pours into the record like a dollop of sunscreen. And there isn’t an alligator in sight! Mason explores Florida and what it means to live there, challenging perceptions of endless sunshine, bars, beaches, and Mickey Mouse ears – the Humidity Kingdom and not the Magic Kingdom – and echoing novelist Lauren Groff’s collection of short stories, ‘Florida’, with its humid atmosphere. A state where ‘everybody is sleeping save for the tree frogs and the sinners’. Panthers, bears, snakes, mosquitos, gators; it’s a deadly place. The land is capable of a deluge of rain, curtailing baseball games and adding to the state’s exotic vibe. But a still clarity exists inside the music, along with an absence of people, like an empty stretch of highway or a shopping mall before opening hours. The microscopic tones seem to thrive in the heat, which is the opposite of a UK tourist in the Everglades, where skin burns and peels instantaneously, a vampire exposed to midday sun. Mason uses guitar and tape – where sensitive melodies are sketched in a lo-fi environment, sleepily sitting on a porch in the late afternoon – and creates a pleasant warmth, and its sunshine is more than welcome. Within these tiny tones and a drenched atmosphere, Mason explores and engages with ideas of synthesis and the bio-feedback of plants, creating organic and naturally-flowing music. The second release, Plains, by John Atkinson and Talya Cooper, was inspired by ‘the open skies of the West’, its arid nature is a sharp contrast to the Floridian swamps, the orange groves, and the gushing waters of its East Coast sister, but the music is no less ambient, and they share common ground in the rising of its temperatures. Plains takes elements from the original score of ‘Two Plains & A Fancy’, the third film from Lev Kalman and Whitney Horn, which was described by The New Yorker as ‘the most imaginative and visionary’ Western film of recent years. Cooper’s guitar lightly punctures the soundscape while Atkinson takes on processing duties, allowing the music to shift and sway in the lightest of April winds. It blooms without any sharp edges, and all of the composition’s elements are brought into one. It isn’t constricted music, despite the glaring heat or the threat of dehydration or the boa-constrictor of an imminent headache gripping the skull and squeezing against bone. No, this is wide-open music, just as the desert is and always will be, as sparse as an old and vacant town, whose inhabitants all left for better things a long time ago, and downtown consists of a bar and a motel. Sometimes, it’s worth taking a step back, distancing oneself from the chaos of the world and choosing meditation over mania, and the music offers this as a safe space, a place for outstretched arms in an area free of the gravity of others. Like the West, it lives as an outsider, on the edge of things, but it’s a serene oasis, and that’s about as close to a definition of ambient as one can get. As it distances itself, it has the strange paradox of zooming in, of forming a deep concentration. It’s a record of exploratory beauty. Both releases focus on the atmosphere of place via a subtle tweaking of tones and a light ambient coasting. ‘Cloudless’ introduces faint guitar arpeggios and splayed chords specked with ‘verb. The light doesn’t just shine through – it arrives in a flood of warmth, not just dappling but eclipsing the valleys and dust-bowls, the clifftops and mountains. The music is in love with its Western environment, almost dedicating its sound to its natural, awestruck geography. Shaped over a million years and more, the music can only succumb to its widespread lands, the blazing azure of its skies, and the endless, flat horizon. Even as the drones fade away, they leave behind a dying warmth which continues to affect the record, lingering on the face like the sun’s afterglow. These two releases allow for a time-out and a virtual vacation. Be sure to check out more of Florabelle’s quietly moving discography. www.florabelle.bandcamp.com
items._cn_summary: 本文介绍Florabelle厂牌即将发行的两张氛围音乐专辑。Josh Mason的《Coquina Dose》以吉他与磁带为媒介，在lo-fi质感中构建出佛州潮湿气候的声景，微观音色如同正午蜻蜓般悬浮于池水涟漪之上，挑战人们对阳光之州的刻板印象，音乐与植物生物反馈理念交融。John Atkinson与Talya Cooper合作的《Plains》取材自西部片《Two Plains & A Fancy》原声，Cooper的吉他轻点声景，Atkinson负责处理，两人在四月微风中编织出无棱角的辽阔西部天空。两张作品虽地理与气候意象迥异，却在氛围脉络与温度上升的感知上形成呼应，独立小厂牌气质鲜明。

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑聚焦乌克兰被俄罗斯强制带走的约两万儿童这一战争罪行，以传统民歌与原创作品交织的方式呈现。乌克兰-加拿大歌手Marichka联合两组音乐人，一组在乌克兰、一组在加拿大，以全女性阵容Daughters of Donbas巡回演出。器乐以弓弦乐器为主，辅以班杜拉琴和钢琴，还邀请来自被摧毁城市马里乌波尔的Lisa用双陶笛演奏独奏——她曾是十六岁被劫走的儿童之一。曲目《Foreign Land》取材于传统民歌，讲述少女被迫远赴异乡打工的故事，与当下被拐儿童的命运形成对照，歌词质朴而沉痛。《Rusalka》则转向严厉粗砺的基调，借鉴乌克兰传统仪式歌曲中的水妖意象。专辑在音乐品质和人声表现上都达到了较高水准，将地方传统与当代议题紧密结合。

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items._cn_summary: 这是一张芬兰手风琴与钢琴二重奏专辑，源于两位音乐家长达三十五年的合作关系。两人发展出高度的默契与即兴直觉，演奏中常见的传统曲目与原创作品并存，结构简洁，以旋律本身为核心。手风琴的歌唱性旋律线与钢琴的和声支撑相互交织，整体氛围宁静、流畅，带有梦幻般的质感。曲目编排包含北欧传统曲、Piazzolla 的探戈风格作品以及原创芬兰探戈，并偶尔加入弦乐四重奏扩展音色。两人并不追求炫技式的炫示，而是致力于探索旋律本身的内在美感。乐评认为作品虽不会带来强烈冲击，却呈现出一种纯粹的听觉之美。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?

items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自丹麦三人组合的首张数字EP，由北欧民谣场景中经验丰富的歌手Mia Guldhammer领衔。五首曲目大多基于传统音乐素材，乐手各自带入不同视角。开场曲粗粝的奔跑节奏为Guldhammer的嗓音提供了展示窗口；唯一的原创曲目由乐队成员Morten Musicus创作，口簧与风笛带来强烈的推进感。传统曲目中加入匈牙利扬琴作为细腻的声底，器乐终曲则将口簧与长笛、弦乐交织，产生奇异而不失刺激的听觉效果。整体呈现出古老而略显斑驳的氛围，五首曲目已展现出乐队超越新人阶段的成熟度。

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由瑞典小提琴手与两位挪威乐手合作，选取斯堪的纳维亚传统舞曲素材，但放弃了舞蹈功能，转而走向室内乐式的亲密对话。三位乐手均长期探索跨界融合：小提琴家Edén横跨演奏、作曲与教学；Tellef Kvifte使用竖笛、萨克斯与风笛等非常规乐器；其子Nesheim作为鼓手与作曲家致力于模糊流派边界。专辑以挪威Setesdal山谷的传说旋律"Fossgrimen"开场，暗示小提琴源自水妖、带有魔鬼乐器色彩等北欧民间音乐中的幽暗底蕴。在瑞典曲"Polska from Per Myhr"中，三人以解构方式展开：竖笛反复引子、小提琴提供模糊质感伴奏、鼓声零星点缀，随后旋律统一出现又骤然崩解消散。整体呈现出对传统素材深层含义的重新审视，既保留地域文化的暗流气质，又通过自由即兴与结构碎裂实现当代演绎。

items.body: Review by arcane-beautiful — Singularity & Other Stories by Echoes & Signals is another great album from the Russian proggers that shows off great songwriting and technical ability, but it doesn't have the impact of the first album they released this year. While Solar saw the band put forward their strongest material to date, this album is similar in tone but I think it's the short length that brings it down. But having Leo Margarit provide drumming is a massive bonus, as his work with Pain Of Salvation is exceptional and it's just as impressive on this album. With creative use of synths and vocals, overall it still is a great presentation of the band's sound. I'd give this a mid 7 out of 10. The track I'd recommend is Singularity.
items._cn_summary: 俄罗斯乐队Echoes and Signals在2026年发行的第二张专辑延续了此前作品的气质基调，在作曲技巧与器乐演奏层面表现出扎实功力。专辑邀请了曾与Pain of Salvation合作的鼓手Leo Margarit参与录制，其打击乐编排成为亮点之一，节奏层次复杂且富有推动力。合成器的运用颇具创意，配合人声编排构建出层次丰富的声场。然而，乐评指出专辑篇幅偏短，在冲击力与完整度上不及同年首张专辑《Solar》，整体听感虽精致却未能充分展开。推荐曲目为标题曲《Singularity》。该作品在技术层面值得肯定，但风格上偏向传统器乐摇滚谱系，与极端实验或前卫跨界路线尚有距离。

items.body: Chicago post-punk trio French Police released the double single “Super Over Drive” / “Silver” on 28 August 2026 through Interscope Records, with a video for each track. “Super Over Drive” and “Silver” are the band’s second release for the label, four weeks after the “Reptile” / “Japan” double single that opened the deal. Chris Eichenseer directed both clips as a Someoddpilot Studios production and also shot the cover art. The “Super Over Drive” video puts the trio through a sepia-toned performance in which bodies blur into movement and faces appear and disappear. What French Police put on ‘Super Over Drive’ and ‘Silver’ “Super Over Drive” runs 3:22 and rides a driving bass line while Manny Herrera’s guitar cuts back into the arrangement from shifting angles. Brian Flores stretches his phrasing further than on earlier French Police tracks, holding notes past the point where the delivery stays composed. “Silver” runs 3:04, opens the arrangement out and leaves more space around the vocal, trading the first track’s defensiveness for a direct admission. Both tracks are on Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer and the other streaming services. No album has been announced around them, so they stand as the band’s second standalone Interscope single. The pairing follows “Reptile” / “Japan”, which arrived at the end of July 2026 and was the trio’s first release for a major label after seven years of self-released records and vinyl through independents. Side-Line reported that release in French Police signs to Interscope Records, releases ‘Reptile / Japan’ double single. The Mexican-American singer, songwriter and guitarist writes in Spanish and English. Manny Herrera plays lead guitar and Rolando Donjuan plays bass. The trio bring a post-punk that mixes chorused guitar lines, driving bass and coldwave-leaning vocals, and they share a listener base with Lebanon Hanover, Molchat Doma and The Chameleons. The self-titled debut appeared in 2019, followed by the “Pedaleo Nocturno” EP the same year and the 15-track “Haunted Castle” in February 2020, which Icy Cold Records later pressed to CD. A dense run of self-released EPs and singles followed through 2021 and 2022, among them “Pensamiento Negro”, “Onyx” and “1995”, with “Club De Vampiros / Plant Based Girl” issued by Icy Cold Records in January 2022 and “Fumar / Hate Me” by Cruel Records that May. “Bleu” arrived in February 2023, and Audiotree released a live single and EP the following month. “Bully” came out on 26 January 2024, again self-released digitally with a vinyl edition through Icy Cold Records. Side-Line covered those European pressings in French Police launch limited European vinyl editions of ‘Bully’ and ‘Haunted Castle’, and Side-Line reviewed the album in French Police – Haunted Castle (Album – Icy Cold Records). The “Espera” EP followed in January 2025 with the singles “Sugar Killer” and “Libra” later that year, and Icy Cold Records collected earlier material on the “Essentials” CD in March 2026. The Interscope deal, announced at the end of July 2026, ends the self-released period; “Super Over Drive” and “Silver” are the first songs the band has put out since the tour was announced.

items.body: Toronto coldwave duo Traitrs released the official video for “I Was Ill, You Were Wrong” on 28 August 2026, a month before they open a ten-date US run in Dallas. The track first appeared as a standalone single on 28 November 2025 and became the second song on “POSSESSOR”, the fourth Traitrs album, issued through Furniture Records on 13 March 2026. Shawn Tucker directed the video and shot it in black and white on location in a studio warehouse in Hamilton, Ontario. Emmanuelle Vaughan plays the lead, Daniel Cherney worked as first assistant director, and Tucker and Cherney shared camera duties. What Shawn Tucker says about the ‘I Was Ill, You Were Wrong’ video Tucker connects the shoot to a death in his own life and to the way the album was written. “This album is incredibly personal for me because I’m still trying to make sense of a major loss in my own life,” he said. “When I directed this, the goal was to visualize death as this unstoppable force, almost like a terminal illness creeping through the body. It doesn’t care who you are; it just destroys. But I didn’t want the video to just be bleak. It’s about our internal fight.” The set is a black chamber with no walls, floor or horizon. Vaughan appears under a single overhead light, an oil-dark coating spreads across her hands, arms, back and throat, and she keeps moving until the frame empties. Tucker cast her after working with her on the earlier “Burn In Heaven” video and named Jonathan Glazer’s film “Under the Skin” as the reference for the space. “The void represented Ultimate Isolation perfectly and supports my visual theme of total isolation,” Tucker said. “There are no walls, no horizons, and no exit. The victims are entirely alone with their desires right before they are destroyed.” He described the shoot in plain terms: “It was all shot in one day on location in a small studio warehouse in Hamilton, Ontario, that took 7 hours.” When the song came out in November 2025, Tucker linked it to a shared recognition rather than a private one. “I felt that song connected me to everything and everyone, it is the one thing we all share and have in common,” he said. “It is also a wake up call to live the life you want to live. We only have one chance at this so go dance in the rain.” Traitrs ‘POSSESSOR’ formats and credits Traitrs recorded “POSSESSOR” at Wychwood in Toronto with long-time collaborator Josh Korody, who co-produced. Matt Colton mastered the album at Metropolis Mastering, and Tucker supplied the artwork. Furniture Records pressed the Canadian edition as a black LP limited to 400 copies, plus CD and a limited cassette. Icy Cold Records handled the first European edition on cream white vinyl with an insert, limited to 500 copies, and a CD digipak. Side-Line covered both announcements in Traitrs set March 13 release for fourth album ‘Possessor’ and confirm 2026 North American tour and Icy Cold to launch Traitrs ‘Possessor’ EU edition on cream white vinyl. The physical editions run ten tracks: “Burn In Heaven”, “I Was Ill, You Were Wrong”, “Seven Fictions”, “Cold Skin”, “Selfish Hunger”, “Prayertaker”, “Dream Drowning”, “Mourn”, “Japanese Picture Pony” and “Crawl”. “Burn In Heaven” got its own video on 12 March 2026, the day before the album arrived. Traitrs tour dates 2026 The US run opens on 29 September in Dallas and closes on 16 October in Washington, DC. 29 September 2026 – Dallas, TX, US – Club Dada 30 September 2026 – Austin, TX, US – Elysium 1 October 2026 – Pomona, CA, US – Flyway 6 October 2026 – Las Vegas, NV, US – The Dive Bar 8 October 2026 – Fresno, CA, US – Fulton 55 9 October 2026 – San José, CA, US – The Ritz 10 October 2026 – Sacramento, CA, US – The Starlet Room at Harlow’s 13 October 2026 – Raleigh, NC, US – The Pour House 14 October 2026 – Atlanta, GA, US – The Drunken Unicorn 16 October 2026 – Washington, DC, US – Pie Shop About Traitrs Traitrs formed in Toronto in late 2015 as a recording project built around Shawn Tucker on vocals and guitar and Sean-Patrick Nolan on keyboards and writing. Sessions with producer Josh Korody produced the debut “Rites and Ritual” in 2016, released on the Toronto label Pleasence Records as a cassette and reissued on CD and vinyl over the following years by Alchera Visions, Furniture Records and Icy Cold Records. “Butcher’s Coin” followed on 18 May 2018, issued jointly by Manic Depression, Alchera Visions and Pleasence Records. Its track “Thin Flesh” was used in Lionsgate’s 2024 remake of “The Crow”. The third album, “Horses in the Abattoir”, arrived on 19 November 2021 through Freakwave, with CD, cassette and coloured vinyl variants in 2021 and 2022 and a US reissue on Metropolis Records on opaque tangerine vinyl in October 2025. Touring has taken the duo through more than a dozen countries, including Wave-Gotik-Treffen, Castle Party and Canadian Music Week, plus dates with VNV Nation, Lebanon Hanover, She Past Away, Twin Tribes and Ultra Sunn. Side-Line reported on the 2024 North American shows in VNV Nation launches extra North American tour dates with Traitrs. After a four-year gap, the band returned in September 2025 with the “Burn In Heaven” single, followed by “I Was Ill, You Were Wrong” that November and “POSSESSOR” in March 2026. The new video is the second clip pulled from that album and lands as the autumn US dates approach.

items.body: Patience is among the stranger disciplines of love because it asks a person to remain near suffering without assuming the authority to cure it. Anyone may promise companionship while happiness is plentiful; greater difficulty begins when another person withdraws behind pain that cannot be reached by affection, argument, or sacrifice. There comes a terrible education in understanding that love has limits, and that another person’s life, however precious, cannot finally be lived on their behalf. San Diego trio Twin Ritual enters that difficult territory with Suffocate, a synth-pop song concerned with the anguish of watching someone disappear inward while continuing to offer them a place beside you. Vocalist Hannah Mahute, joined by Anthony Ramirez of Glass Spells on synthesizers and drums and Antonio Estrada on guitar, gives the song an expansive emotional scale without sacrificing the small, private quality of its subject. Ramirez establishes a firm rhythmic foundation beneath broad synthesizer lines whose melodic rise gives the song its forward pull. Estrada’s guitar hangs across the arrangement in spacious, carefully measured phrases, sometimes adding texture and elsewhere carrying a melody of its own. These elements create considerable breadth around Mahute, whose voice occupies the center with a softness capable of becoming suddenly severe. She sings as though each sentence has been considered before being spoken, aware that carelessly chosen words can wound someone already retreating from the world. Love here contains patience, tenderness, frustration, and the humiliating recognition that devotion cannot perform another person’s healing. There is no shortage of affection in wanting to carry someone else’s burden, yet such generosity can quietly become an attempt to govern their suffering. Eventually one must acknowledge the boundary between standing beside another person and following them into their destruction. The drums maintain their determined pace while synthesizer hooks open above them and Estrada’s guitar provides a cool, melodic counterweight. That physical momentum gives the emotional paralysis at the song’s center a sharp contradiction: everything moves while one person remains trapped inside themselves. Unconditional love is something more difficult than endless endurance. Sometimes love means waiting without judgement and leaving a portal open; sometimes it means accepting that no amount of tenderness can rescue somebody unwilling or unable to reach for the hand extended toward them. Twin Ritual finds its deepest ache in that knowledge, where patience finally meets the limits of power. Listen to Suffocate below and order the single here. items._cn_summary: Twin Ritual 的单曲《Suffocate》以合成器流行与后朋克的语汇，探讨陪伴他人穿越痛苦时爱所遭遇的边界。Hannah Mahute 的演唱居于中心，声音柔软却可在瞬间转为冷峻，仿佛每个词都经过斟酌后才被说出。Anthony Ramirez 以合成器铺设宽广的旋律线条，配合稳定的节奏推进；Antonio Estrada 的吉他以疏朗的乐句横贯编曲，既提供质感纹理，也独立承担旋律走向。歌曲在情感层面呈现一种矛盾：外在的音乐流动不断向前，内在却困锁于停滞。整首作品没有追求极端实验，而是以成熟的暗潮基底承载严肃的情感议题，对偏好暗潮与后朋克氛围的听众具有吸引力，但在声音创新层面相对克制。

items.body: Oxford has certain ghosts to answer for. The Thames Valley once produced a generation of guitar bands who treated distortion less as decoration than physical substance, something capable of swallowing melody and returning it in stranger shapes. Violet Oscillation comes from that same ground, and on their debut EP, it has become clear to me that all those who seek sounds deeply aware of the inheritance without behaving like a museum exhibit dedicated to 1991. Across five densely layered songs, guitars buckle, blur, bend sideways, then dissolve into banks of reverb where the human voice becomes another instrument caught inside the machinery. Veil establishes the method with glide guitar bent into great slabs of pitch and pressure. The My Bloody Valentine connection is obvious, yet Violet Oscillation understands that imitation begins where curiosity ends. Their guitars keep shifting underfoot, with chords smeared across one another until melody appears almost accidentally through the distortion. The track has tremendous weight, though its movement remains oddly weightless, as if the amplifier stacks had somehow learned to levitate. All Meaning Was Whole pushes further into that overloaded guitar language. Layers accumulate until individual parts become difficult to isolate, which is precisely where the song becomes interesting. There are melodies buried everywhere, rising briefly from the mass before being folded back into it. The performance has the strange emotional scale that made shoegaze compelling in the first place: private feeling blown up to architectural dimensions, bedroom uncertainty projected across a wall of amplifiers. Primordial Learning, featuring Abstract in Sound, shifts toward the airier end of Violet Oscillation’s vocabulary. Slowdive and Cocteau Twins hover somewhere in the ancestry, particularly in the suspended vocals and soft-focus guitar treatments, while the arrangement maintains a restless interior motion. Voices drift through overlapping effects, guitars hang in elongated chords, and each new layer seems to widen the room by another impossible few feet. Ethereal, featuring Abstract in Sound, maintains Slowdive’s gauzy style with a slow-moving layer of dreamy haze that resonates with an otherworldly, euphoric energy. It flutters, with stereo channels moving apart and together, creating a calming yet disorienting effect, reminiscent of floating upward and descending toward murmuring angels, or entering a parallel universe. The song smoothly shifts to a gentle marching drum beat as it fades away. Visual Snow closes the EP in a thick blur of texture, melody, and accumulated noise. The title fits: everything seems visible yet unstable, as though the music were being perceived through an electrical haze. Lovesliescrushing provides another useful reference point here, especially in the manner that guitar becomes atmosphere, mass, and motion simultaneously. Violet Oscillation have spent years embedded in shoegaze culture through Pedal Partners, signature effects pedals, and connections extending from Kevin Shields’ Fender Blender launch to Slowdive’s Simon Scott. None of that biography would mean much if these songs could not carry themselves. Fortunately, they can. it has become clear to me that all those who seek finds Violet Oscillation treating shoegaze as a living vocabulary: guitars bent beyond polite recognition, voices suspended inside great clouds of amplification, and four songs determined to discover how much feeling can be packed into distortion before the speakers finally surrender. items._cn_summary: 这张EP延续了牛津吉他乐队对失真与回响的传统，开篇以滑棒吉他铺设音墙，随后层层堆叠到旋律几乎被噪音吞噬的密度。人声在混响中不再作为主角，而是融入器乐肌理。作品在音色上受到My Bloody Valentine、Slowdive与Cocteau Twins的明显影响，但并非简单复刻：失真和弦交错涂抹，旋律从混沌中偶然浮现，慢板曲目则拓展空间感，利用立体声分离制造漂浮般的失重体验。结尾以密集的纹理与积累的噪音收束，模糊了旋律与声音物质的界限。整体是类型内部扎实但偏向致敬谱系的创作，器乐探索有余而突破性框架创新有限，对暗潮与实验口味的听众来说属于可触但非核心交集的范畴。

items.body: Every track has a voice on it this time. Trentemøller releases trentemøller, his self-titled album, on 13 November 2026 through his own label In My Room, on red vinyl, CD, cassette and digital. The first single, Terrified, arrived on 28 August with a video directed by Jonas Bjerre of the Danish band Mew, who also sings on it. It is the first Trentemøller album on which every one of the ten songs carries vocals. trentemøller by Trentemøller Inside the new Trentemøller album The running order is “Swerve”, “Terrified”, “Visceral”, “Johnny Boy”, “Halved”, “Your Love Walks Alone”, “To Mist”, “Coyote”, “Crash” and “White Hallways”. Anders Trentemøller wrote, played, produced and mixed the record himself and released it on his own label. The guest list runs through the tracklist: Vienna-based singer Sakura on “Swerve” and “Visceral”, Anika on “Johnny Boy”, Bjerre on “Terrified”, Sune Rose Wagner of The Raveonettes on “Your Love Walks Alone” and Madeline Johnston, who records as Midwife, on “Halved”, with Tan Cologne and Emma Acs also appearing. Acs now sings in his live band. Trentemøller described how he cut the album down: “The noisy got noisier, the dreamy got dreamier, the melodic got even more melodic. I was ruthless this time. Okay, kill your darlings! If a track didn’t give me a feeling of freedom, wanderlust, sorrow, love or that pure ‘I don’t give a fuck’ feeling … It was gone.” “Terrified” runs three minutes and was rebuilt after the fact. On the change he made to it, Trentemøller said: “‘Terrified’ is probably the poppiest song on the album. In its original form it sounded a lot more shoegazey, but I wanted it to be crisper and clearer, less washed out. So I went for synths that almost sound like human voices, with a magical, otherworldly quality to them. When the instrumental was done, I sent it to Jonas Bjerre with a few melody ideas, which he took further while adding new melodies of his own.” Bjerre wrote the lyrics and explained where they came from: “I think sometimes when you dream about things that make you fearful and uneasy, it’s your mind trying to prepare you for any scenario, like you’re processing catastrophes that have not and may not ever happen.” He also shot and compiled the video, with cinematography shared with Sarah Liisborg, and Mackenzie Stith, Yuting Liu and Agnete Hegelund appearing in it. Trentemøller tour dates 2027 The full band play fourteen European shows in February and March 2027, opening in Berlin and closing at home in Copenhagen, with two nights at Ancienne Belgique in Brussels. Trentemøller said he intends to play the album in full on the run: “Now I can’t wait to play these songs live with my band. For the first time ever, I’m going to play the whole album, start to end. Every single song!” 27.02.2027 – Berlin, DE – Huxley’s Neue Welt 01.03.2027 – Munich, DE – Kesselhaus 02.03.2027 – Bern, CH – Bierhübeli 03.03.2027 – Paris, FR – La Cigale 05.03.2027 – Brussels, BE – Ancienne Belgique 06.03.2027 – Brussels, BE – Ancienne Belgique 07.03.2027 – Luxembourg, LU – Den Atelier 09.03.2027 – Amsterdam, NL – Paradiso 11.03.2027 – London, UK – Electric Ballroom 13.03.2027 – Cologne, DE – Carlswerk Victoria 17.03.2027 – Oslo, NO – Rockefeller 18.03.2027 – Gothenburg, SE – Pustervik 19.03.2027 – Stockholm, SE – Slaktkyrkan 20.03.2027 – Copenhagen, DK – VEGA About Trentemøller Anders Trentemøller was born on 16 October 1972 and works from Copenhagen. He came out of the Danish club scene in the early 2000s and released his debut album “The Last Resort” in October 2006 on Poker Flat Recordings, a record built on slow, textured electronics rather than dancefloor tempos. He founded his own label, In My Room, around 2010 and has released everything since through it. “Into the Great Wide Yonder” arrived on 28 May 2010 and pulled guitars and live drums into the arrangements. “Lost” followed in September 2013 with a long guest list, then “Fixion” in September 2016 and “Obverse” on 27 September 2019. “Memoria” came out on 11 February 2022, trailed by the singles “In the Gloaming”, “All Too Soon” and “No More Kissing in the Rain”, and Side-Line reviewed it on release. “Dreamweaver”, with vocals by Dísa Jakobs throughout, followed on 13 September 2024. Alongside his own records he has remixed widely. Side-Line has reported on his 2022 reworking of Blood’s “Type 9000” and on his 2025 remix of “And Nothing Is Forever” for The Cure‘s “Mixes of a Lost World”. Side-Line also reported in 2023 that he was among the acts announced to support Depeche Mode on their European tour. The self-titled album on 13 November is his first since “Dreamweaver”.
items._cn_summary: Trentemøller 即将发行同名专辑，收录十首全部带有人声的歌曲，这是他首次尝试全人声配置。制作人 Anders Trentemøller 独自完成词曲、演奏、制作及混音，通过自有厂牌 In My Room 发行红胶、CD、卡带及数字版本。首支单曲《Terrified》与丹麦乐队 Mew 主唱 Jonas Bjerre 合作，Bjerre 撰写歌词并执导MV，歌曲从原本的 shoegaze 质感被改造成更清脆通透的合成器流行曲风。专辑邀请多位客座歌手参与，包括 Sakura、Anika、The Raveonettes 的 Sune Rose Wagner 以及 Midwife 等。Trentemøller 表示在制作过程中追求更极端的动态对比——噪音更噪、梦幻更梦幻、旋律更突出，剔除无法带来自由、忧郁或爱之感受的作品。2027年他将携完整乐队在欧洲进行十四场巡演，首次完整演绎新专辑曲目。

items.body: Texan electro-industrial act Mentallo & The Fixer see their 1994 album “Where Angels Fear To Tread” reissued by Re:Mission Entertainment on 16 October 2026. The record has never appeared on vinyl before: this edition arrives as a 2LP gatefold pressed on yellow and red inverted splatter vinyl, limited to 250 copies worldwide. Discogs lists no prior vinyl pressing in any territory. Both formats carry a new remaster by Jeff Mortimer at JM Mastering. The edition also restores the album’s original 1994 artwork, replacing the new cover the record was given for its last reissue; the artwork restoration and vinyl layout are credited to Nathan Winter at Industriarts. The vinyl gatefold prints the full lyrics alongside commentary from Gary Dassing on the making of the record. Re:Mission estimates the LP will ship on 20 November and sells it through the band’s own Big Cartel store, where a line of shirts, hoodies, tanks and posters accompanies it. The digital edition is on pre-order at Bandcamp now and reaches streaming and download platforms on 16 October. Re:Mission states the reissue exists because “it’s been important for Re:Mission to maintain high quality restorations of the original art and proper masters”, and describes the aim as bringing the record back “for the fans who’ve kept it in rotation all these years”. Where Angels Fear To Tread by Mentallo & The Fixer What the two Mentallo & The Fixer editions hold The vinyl runs to 15 tracks and the digital edition to 20. One point needs flagging: Re:Mission describes the LP as the original thirteen tracks plus two remixes, while Discogs and Wikipedia both list the 1994 Zoth Ommog CD as a fourteen-track album whose closing piece is already “Sacrilege (Grimpen Ward)”. The digital running order is: “Gargantua” “Decomposed (Trampled)” “Sacrilege” “Virtually Hopeless” “Bring To A Boil” “Coward (Submerged)” “Ruthless” “Afterglow” “Battered States Of Euphoria” “Abominations Unleashed” “Dead Days” “Atom Smasher” “Power Struggle” “Sacrilege (Grimpen Ward)” “Decomposed (Grimpen Ward)” “Sacrilege (Angel Of Death Mix)” “Decomposed (Original Mix)” “Rapid Suffocation (Lesionary Mix)” “Grim Reality (Blister Mix)” “Battered States Of Euphoria (Medina Mix)” The “Grimpen Ward” tag on tracks 14 and 15 is a remix name the brothers used during their Zoth Ommog years, and it predates the 2001 album of that name. A “Decomposed (Grimpen Ward Mix)” was already circulating on the 1995 Ras Dva compilation “There Is No Time”. The 1994 album and the editions that came before this one “Where Angels Fear To Tread” first appeared on 16 May 1994 on the German label Zoth Ommog, then a division of Music Research. Metropolis Records licensed it from Zoth Ommog and issued it in North America on 18 July 1995 with the same running order and no extra material. The album carries “Decomposed”, “Sacrilege” and “Atom Smasher”, the three tracks that reached club sets. Its most recent outing was as part of “Zothera”, the 3CD box Alfa Matrix issued in September 2014, which paired a remastered “Where Angels Fear To Tread” with a remastered “Revelations 23” and a disc of unreleased remixes titled “Apocrypha”. That box came with new cover art, which is what the 2026 edition reverses. About Mentallo & The Fixer Mentallo & The Fixer are the Texan brothers Gary Dassing, who takes the Mentallo half of the name, and Dwayne Dassing, who takes The Fixer. The two had been buying synthesizers since the mid-1980s and first recorded together in San Antonio as Benestrophe, a trio completed by vocalist Richard Mendez, whom Gary met in his final year of high school. Benestrophe cut its first song, “Pig Butcher”, in the summer of 1988 and went quiet in 1990 when the Dassings moved to Austin, where the brothers restarted as Mentallo & The Fixer. The debut album “No Rest For The Wicked” came out in 1992 on the Portuguese label Simbiose Records. “Revelations 23” followed in February 1993, the first of their records for Zoth Ommog, with Metropolis handling the US edition in 1995. “Where Angels Fear To Tread” arrived in 1994, the same year as the remix set “Mentallo & The Fixer Meets Mainesthai”. Benestrophe was revived after 1995 for the Ras Dva label, which released “Auric Fires” in 1997, and Alfa Matrix later collected that project’s archive as “Turner’s All Night Drugstore (Rare & Unreleased 1987-1997)” in 2018, covered here at the time. Dwayne Dassing left after 1997’s “Burnt Beyond Recognition”, and Gary Dassing continued alone through “Algorythum” (1999), “Love Is The Law” (2000), “Return To Grimpen Ward” and “Vengeance Is Mine” (both 2001), “Enlightenment Through A Chemical Catalyst” (2007), “Music From The Eather” (2012) and “Arrange The Molecule” (2017). Re:Mission Entertainment, which opened an official Mentallo And The Fixer merch store in 2021, has been working through the catalogue since. It put out “No Rest For The Wicked” as a 30th-anniversary edition in October 2022, a “Vengeance Is Mine” remaster in June 2025 and a 25th-anniversary “Love Is The Law” in September 2025. The label also released “Thorns”, the 2024 debut album by Dwayne Dassing’s Reign Of Roses. The brothers reunited as a duo in early 2025, when they announced a new album and their first US tour since 2006. The tour ran from September to November 2025 and took in ColdWaves XIII in Chicago, dates on the Industrial Nation run alongside Front Line Assembly, Clock DVA, Lead Into Gold and Nitzer Ebb, and a Resurrection Tour leg with labelmates Pygmy Children. No title, tracklist or release date has been made public for that new studio album since the February 2025 announcement, and this reissue is a catalogue release rather than the record announced then.
items._cn_summary: 这张1994年专辑首次以黑胶形式再版，由Re:Mission Entertainment以黄红交错溅射彩胶双LP形式发行，全球限量250张。Jeff Mortimer完成全新母带处理，Nathan Winter恢复了原始1994年封面设计与歌词印刷。数字版扩充至20首，包含多首Grimpen Ward混音及此前未公开的混音作品。Mentallo & The Fixer作为德州电子工业组合，在Zoth Ommog厂牌时期形成了鲜明的合成器工业声响，混音作品以层次分明的电子脉冲与机械节奏构建压迫感。Re:Mission以小型独立厂牌姿态强调母带品质与艺术修复，面向多年持续关注此作的核心听众。

items.body: Chilean band Amöniacö released the single “En algún momento” on 27 August 2026, the second track lifted from the re-recorded version of their 2011 debut album “Tu Fuego”. Carlos Vandal and Felipe Alarcón wrote the song, Vandal produced it at Noiser Studio in Santiago, and Fernando Cubillos mastered it at Riot Diva Studio. The song is not new. It sat fifth on the original “Tu Fuego”, released in October 2011, an album the band has said never got the promotion it needed at the time. Across 2025 and 2026 Amöniacö re-recorded, remixed and remastered the whole record, and a vinyl edition of the new version is planned. “En algún momento” follows “Aprendo a Morir (Sudden death version)”, issued on 8 May 2026 as the first preview, and pairs the same treatment with a restoration of the band’s earliest audiovisual material. Amöniacö mix alternative rock with post-punk and darkwave, and this track leans on the more atmospheric end of that: layered guitars, melodic lines and a driving rhythm underneath. The lyric deals with memories that return without permission, and with what stays behind after someone has gone. The single is on Spotify and across digital stores. It has not been posted to the band’s Bandcamp page, where the rest of the catalogue sits. What the Amöniacö ‘Tu Fuego’ relaunch covers The relaunch is a full re-recording rather than a remaster of the 2011 tapes. Every song from the original eleven-track album is being redone, with Vandal handling production at Noiser Studio and Cubillos mastering, the same pairing behind both singles released so far. Alongside the audio work, the band has restored the video material that goes with the earliest songs. The vinyl pressing has been confirmed but not dated. About Amöniacö Amöniacö began in the mid-2000s with Carlos Vandal writing the first songs, and put its first track, “Aprendo a Morir”, online in 2006. The band was formally constituted in Santiago de Chile in 2008. The current line-up is Vandal on vocals, guitars, bass and sequences, and Rod García on drums; the 2011 recordings featured Vandal with Jano Perverso on bass and Gabrielle on keyboards. The debut album “Tu Fuego” arrived in October 2011 with limited distribution. In 2012 the band reached the final of the Peugeot Music platform, and in April 2013 it opened for The Cure at the Estadio Nacional in Santiago on the group’s Latin American tour, selected by Robert Smith, who chose the support acts for each country himself. The single “Time to Change” followed, recorded and mixed by British engineer Barry Sage and mastered by Martin Bowes at The Cage Studios in Coventry. In 2015 Amöniacö played Lima with Cardenales and was selected for the third Converse Rubber Tracks call, which produced “No Volveré” with Pablo Giadach at Estudio Lautaro. “Castigarás” was recorded at Indómito Records with André Valenzuela, mastered by Mariano Pavez, played live in November 2017 and released digitally in January 2018. In 2017 the band joined the roster of the Santiago Noiser production company. The “Azul Prusia” EP, produced by José Ignacio Jaras, followed and was later taken into the catalogue of Cleopatra Records in the United States. Through the early 2020s the band issued the singles “Ritos”, “And Then It Rains” and “Regrets”, and in April 2024 opened for Clan of Xymox at Blondie in Santiago. “Live at Unisono”, recorded at Gustavo Cerati’s Estudio Unísono in Buenos Aires and mixed and mastered by Fernando Cubillos, came out in February 2025, and later that year the band issued a version of Soda Stereo’s “Canción Animal” through Scent Air Records. The “Tu Fuego” re-recording began in 2025, and “En algún momento” is its second instalment.
items._cn_summary: 智利乐队Amöniacö发布单曲'En algún momento'，这是其2011年首张专辑'Tu Fuego'重新录制版本的第二首单曲。整张专辑正在进行完整的重新录制、混音和重制，而非简单母带处理，所有十一首曲目均由Carlos Vandal在圣地亚哥Noiser Studio制作，Fernando Cubillos在Riot Diva Studio完成母带处理，计划发行黑胶版本。音乐风格融合另类摇滚、后朋克与暗潮，这首作品偏向氛围化处理，以层叠吉他、旋律线和驱动的节奏为支撑，歌词围绕不请自来的记忆与离去后残留之物展开。乐队成立于2000年代中期的圣地亚哥，2013年曾为The Cure拉丁美洲巡演担任暖场，其发展轨迹涉及独立厂牌与英国工程师合作，具备一定的地下场景背景。

items.body: Buzz Kull released a video for “In the Cut” on 26 August 2026, two weeks before the Sydney project starts a North American tour with Kontravoid. The track comes from “Deep Hate”, the EP Marc Dwyer issued through Heartworm Press on 13 February 2026. Chris Fatseas directed the video, which puts Dwyer opposite Sydney model Andrea. Buzz Kull’s ‘Deep Hate’ EP and its remix edition “Deep Hate” holds four tracks: “Black Gate”, “In The Cut”, “Just A Memory” and “Human Force”. Dwyer wrote and recorded all four, Ewan Kay mixed and mastered them, and Jonathan Schenke added mixing on “In The Cut”. Wes Eisold of Cold Cave sings on “Human Force”, which also carries an additional drum mix by Alex Garcia-Rivera. Amy Lee handled design and Shaun Daniel the photography. Heartworm Press pressed the EP as a 12-inch at 45 RPM in a black-and-white split variant and in a red-and-black marble “Bloodlust” edition limited to 100 copies. The CD and digital editions add four remixes: “Black Gate” reworked by PIG, “In The Cut” by Kontravoid, “Just A Memory” by Cold Cave and “Human Force” by Spike Hellis. Buzz Kull and Kontravoid tour dates The co-headline run opens on 10 September at Elysium in Austin as part of Levitation and closes on 24 October at Below at The Belasco in Los Angeles. Normal Bias supports the Brooklyn show, and Spike Hellis and Normal Bias join the Spokane, Vancouver, Seattle, Portland and Sacramento dates. 10 September 2026 – Austin, TX, US – Elysium (Levitation) 11 September 2026 – Houston, TX, US – Barbarella 12 September 2026 – New Orleans, LA, US – Santos Bar 13 September 2026 – Atlanta, GA, US – The EARL 15 September 2026 – Tampa, FL, US – The Orpheum 16 September 2026 – Orlando, FL, US – Will’s Pub 18 September 2026 – Baltimore, MD, US – Metro Baltimore 19 September 2026 – Philadelphia, PA, US – Nikki Lopez 20 September 2026 – Brooklyn, NY, US – Saint Vitus 22 September 2026 – Montreal, QC, Canada – Foufounes Electriques 24 September 2026 – Toronto, ON, Canada – Cafeteria 25 September 2026 – Millvale, PA, US – The Funhouse at Mr. Smalls 26 September 2026 – Milwaukee, WI, US – Anodyne Coffee Roasting Co. 28 September 2026 – Minneapolis, MN, US – Icehouse 1 October 2026 – Indianapolis, IN, US – The 808 at Indy CD & Vinyl 2 October 2026 – Kansas City, MO, US – Encore at Uptown 3 October 2026 – Denver, CO, US – HQ 4 October 2026 – Salt Lake City, UT, US – Metro Music Hall 6 October 2026 – Spokane, WA, US – The Big Dipper 8 October 2026 – Vancouver, BC, Canada – Biltmore Cabaret 9 October 2026 – Seattle, WA, US – El Corazon 10 October 2026 – Portland, OR, US – Star Theater 13 October 2026 – Reno, NV, US – The Holland Project 15 October 2026 – Sacramento, CA, US – The Starlet Room 16 October 2026 – Las Vegas, NV, US – Backstage Bar & Billiards 23 October 2026 – San Francisco, CA, US – Great American Music Hall (Substance) 24 October 2026 – Los Angeles, CA, US – Below at The Belasco (Substance) Side-Line published the tour announcement in Buzz Kull and Kontravoid announce 2026 North American tour. About Buzz Kull Buzz Kull is the solo project of Sydney musician Marc Dwyer, active since 2012. He mixes darkwave, EBM and minimal synth, and has worked with Rebecca Liston in the live line-up. The project’s first singles, “I Disappear” and “Dreams”, appeared through Fabrika Records in 2013 and 2014. The debut album “Chroma” followed in 2017 and “New Kind of Cross” in 2018, with a run of singles including “Nausea”, “Avoiding The Light”, “Last In The Club”, “Rise From Yur Grave” and “Dancing With Machines” issued through Avant! Records between 2017 and 2022. Side-Line covered the return in Australia’s dark electro act Buzz Kull returns with all new album, the first new work since 2019, which announced the third album “Fascination” on Avant! Records in 2022. Dwyer moved to Eskimo Recordings for the 2023 single “A Place That’s Meant To Be”, then to Cleopatra Records for four singles across 2024 and 2025. “Just A Memory” opened his run on Heartworm Press in 2025 and led into “Deep Hate”, his first release for the label, in February 2026. The “In the Cut” video is the project’s latest, arriving as the North American dates begin.
items._cn_summary: 本文为澳大利亚悉尼项目 Buzz Kull 发布的纯新闻稿，内容围绕其 'In the Cut' 音乐录影带、北美联合巡演及 'Deep Hate' EP 的发行信息展开。文章详细列出了 EP 的四首曲目、混音制作人员名单、黑胶及 CD 版本的发售规格，以及与 Kontravoid 联合巡演的全部场次安排。EP 收录了包含 Cold Cave 主唱 Wes Eisold 献声的合作曲目，CD 版本另附四首分别由 PIG、Kontravoid、Cold Cave 和 Spike Hellis 操刀的混音作品。从音乐内容而言，Buzz Kull 属于暗潮/后朋克/EBM 领域的独立制作，与暗潮音乐偏好契合，但文章本身缺乏任何音乐性分析、声音设计评价或艺术视角讨论，仅为厂牌宣传式的资讯罗列，不具备乐评深度。
