items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items._cn_summary: 这并非传统意义上的专辑乐评，而是一档名为《Racing into the Big Muddy》的电台节目曲目清单。节目以河流与沼泽为主题，串联了Dr John、Johnny Cash、Steve Earle等美国根源音乐艺人，同时纳入芬兰民间音乐（Saly Kouyate、Klakki）、希腊（Martha Mavroidi）、法国（Compagnie Chez Bousca）等欧洲及非洲传统音乐元素，并点缀Jake Blount等当代民谣复兴者的作品。整体呈现为地域性传统音乐与世界民谣的拼盘式编排，缺乏对具体音乐语言、制作手法或艺术构思的评论。由于信息极度有限，仅为节目歌单罗列，无实质性乐评内容可供深入分析。

Twenty years later, this masterpiece stands revealed as a pivotal turning point, says Angus Batey At its simplest, the story of The Roots is about music, musicians and determination. But at the same time – without widening the field of regard substantially – it's also a story of the collapse of the music industry. In other words, the story of the destruction of a business model that, for all its faults, had allowed at least some artists to make a living from recorded music for more than half a century. And while the band's history is still being written – they... The post Undisputed Winners? The Roots’ Game Theory at 20 appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: 本文为The Roots 2006年专辑《Game Theory》发表20周年的回顾文章。文章指出这张作品是乐队的巅峰之作，但在发行时遭遇商业挫折，恰逢音乐行业商业模式的崩塌。该专辑被视为乐队历程中的关键转折点，将嘻哈节奏与爵士器乐、即兴演奏相融合，体现了乐队以原声乐器为基础的独特美学。文章探讨了The Roots如何在没有商业包装支持下坚持音乐创作，以及他们在独立厂牌下保持艺术完整性的历程。由于原文为摘要片段且篇幅极短，具体的音乐分析、曲目拆解及制作细节均缺失，仅提供了专辑的历史定位与行业背景框架，无法深入评判其音乐本体特征。

items.body: Review by arcane-beautiful — Marrow Deep by Mastodon is the band's strongest album in 12 years, with a new take on their sound with new members Nick Johnston & Jo�o Nogueira. The first album not to feature Brent Hinds after his departure then untimely death, lyrically the album deals with loss and the difficulties surrounding it. Overall lyrically it's some of their most poignant and creative. The added use of keyboards to their sound, while present before is now heightened with new member Jo�o Nogueira displaying some nice organ pedals and synth leads, while Nick Johnston has a similar style to the late Hinds, but has a uniqueness in his lead playing. While it's sad not to hear Hinds soulful vocals, Brann Dailor & Troy Sander's vocals are pretty impressive at times, but they do show weakness as well. Musically as always the band are impressive, with moments harkening back to their early Sludge years. While it's not perfect, it's a massive step forward for the band after a slight lull and obvious hardships. I'd give this a high 7 to low 8 out of 10. The track I'd recommend is Serpents For Dinner.
items._genre: progressive metal / sludge metal / heavy rock
items._cn_summary: 这是Mastodon在失去主创Brent Hinds后的首张专辑，主题围绕失去与困境展开。乐队在保留早期sludge金属厚重根基的同时，引入新成员João Nogueira的键盘与合成器层次，Nick Johnston的吉他演奏延续了Hinds的风格但呈现出独立辨识度。Brann Dailor与Troy Sanders的人声表现时而出彩时显薄弱。整体是乐队从沉寂中重新出发的一次尝试，技术扎实但并非具有突破性的实验性作品，与用户偏好的实验前卫、爵士、电子、暗潮等方向相去甚远，属于较为传统的前卫金属范畴内的演进。

items.body: Review by Prog Dog — On my way over to finally dig into Neal Morse's album for my first review, I stumbled across an email I'd overlooked about his brother Alan's recent solo album. My curiosity got the better of me, and I was not disappointed. In fact, I feel like I've made a new guitar friend. Alan is a serious axe player and a very good songwriter to boot, and I've been quite taken by his soulful style and technique throughout this tastefully produced disc. This also proves the lyric from his title track, "Everyday Is Insane." Not really, but thank goodness for spontaneity.This is his second solo album (I haven't yet heard the first), and it's an impressive showcase of the man's very creative and understated solo work. There's very little repetitiveness or redundancy across this collection of eleven tunes, testifying to the abundance of raw source material he is drawing on here. If you're not fond of a song or a moment in a song, just wait a a minute and something completely fresh will come up next. After a few listens I find that I might not be in the mood for a track or two but I generally enjoy it all. He calls on a long list of friends and family to help out on various instruments and background vocals, and there's probably no shortage of familiar names here, least of all his brother Neal (by the way is Neal the big brother? or the little brother??). Tony Levin's presence caught my eye right away. And daughter Julia sings on "Making Up My Heart," which strikes me as a really sweet and personal touch, and a lovely reminder that the line of musical talent runs deep through the Morse family.This is essential listening for any serious Spock's Beard fan, of course, since that's Alan's main gig, and most of the band helps out.To me, though, this is a guitarist's album. Oh, wait, it's a real treat for drummers as well. The drum kits sound amazing and sit tight and loud in the mix throughout, and there's this ripper of a solo at the end of "Making Up My Heart". On the drum throne are some notable players: Simon Phillips, Jimmy Keegan, John Morse and, of course, Nick D'Virgilio.Alan isn't really lead-singer material in the sense of fronting a top-tier band on the world stage, but in a personable singer-songwriter setting, he's more than pleasant company for the ears.Since Alan is proficient in almost any stringed instrument, and he plays more than just guitar on the album. Not sure exactly how many but I heard bouzouki, cello, mandolin, and electric sitar. Not the most attractive album cover, but once you hear what's under the hood, you'll warm right up to it. There are almost party-rock vibes to some of the album, think Van Halen or that unmistakable '80s energy. I hear hints of classic Saga and perhaps '80s Rush as well. It's a thoroughly enjoyable listen for a guitarist and prog fan like me.Prog Dog score: 3.5 out of 5 &/or 3 out of 5 for the progarchives system.
items._cn_summary: Alan Morse作为Spock's Beard吉他手推出的第二张个人专辑，定位为歌手兼词曲作者式的吉他器乐专辑。制作精良，鼓组混音突出，邀请了Tony Levin、Simon Phillips、Nick D'Virgilio等客座乐手。Alan本人演奏多种弦乐器，包括布祖基琴、大提琴、曼陀林和电西塔琴，编曲中融入Van Halen式的派对摇滚气息，并带有80年代Saga和Rush的影子。整体风格偏向传统爵士摇滚融合，技术扎实但叙事保守，缺乏实验性突破。十一首曲目编排多样，避免重复，但音乐语言仍停留在主流前卫摇滚框架内，未触及即兴自由或前卫实验领域。

items.album: DELIRIUM Sesta Strada Lungo il Tempo (Rock Progressivo Italiano, 2026)
items.excerpt: Review by Stefano61 — Genoa keeps its own kind of light, grey and pressed low over the water, the kind that makes a person feel the years passing even when nothing visible has moved. It was in this city, in 1896, that Eugenio Montale was born, long before he went looking elsewhere for words to describe what that light does to a life. He learned early that the sea does not console. It only continues.Something of that same continuing runs through the other Genoese story this record concerns.
items.body: Review by Stefano61 — Genoa keeps its own kind of light, grey and pressed low over the water, the kind that makes a person feel the years passing even when nothing visible has moved. It was in this city, in 1896, that Eugenio Montale was born, long before he went looking elsewhere for words to describe what that light does to a life. He learned early that the sea does not console. It only continues.Something of that same continuing runs through the other Genoese story this record concerns.In 1970 a covers band called I Sagittari became something else when a young man not yet twenty, Ivano Fossati, joined on flute and voice. Delirium, they called themselves from then on, and within a year they had a hit single, Canto di Osanna, and a debut album, Dolce Acqua, poetic and strange enough that one of its songs lifted a dead man's monologue straight out of Spoon River.Then came Jesahel, sung at Sanremo in February of 1972, the five of them arriving, so the story goes, on a bus borrowed from Genoa's own football club. The song made them, for a season, the most hummed tune in the country.It also, by most honest accounts, did the band more harm than good. Barely a season later Fossati was called away to military service and never really came back, choosing instead a solo path that would make him one of the most respected songwriters Italy has produced, one who quietly left the stage in 2012 and has mostly been writing for others ever since.Even Jesahel would not lie still. Only a few years ago it found itself, entirely without anyone's asking, at the center of an international dispute over whether a much younger American voice had borrowed too freely from its melody, proof that these old Genoese tunes still travel further than 1972 could have guessed.An Englishman, Martin Grice, arrived on flute and saxophone to fill the silence Fossati left, and it was largely through him that the band found the sound of Delirium III, Viaggio negli Arcipelaghi del Tempo, a 1974 record already calling time itself an archipelago to be sailed through. Then, like most things Genoese, the band did not end so much as go quiet, and waited.It surfaces now as Delirium International Progressive Group, with Alessandro Corvaglia singing and adding guitar and keyboards, Michele Cusato on guitar, Fabio Chighini on bass, Enrico Tixi on drums.And there, still, are two threads running straight back to the beginning: Ettore Vigo, at the keyboards since that first 1970 lineup, and Martin Grice, on winds since he first stepped into Fossati's silence in 1972. Fifty four years is a long time to keep walking the same road.Sesta Strada Lungo il Tempo, released in May 2026, is in some sense a record about exactly that, about roads and the time that runs alongside them, about how a life, or a band, keeps its shape while everything around it changes.It does not chase anyone's attention. Winds and keyboards still carry most of the weight, as they always have, wrapped now around slower, more patient arrangements and character studies rather than manifestos. The people who populate it are not princes or supermen. They are drifters, the retired, the ones the road passes through rather than the ones who own it, watched with an affection that never curdles into pity.- Schiavo della Vilt�, slave to cowardice, twenty two minutes, nearly an entire vinyl side on its own, and the record's real argument. Cowardice here reads less like a single failing than a paralysis lived quietly for years, and the suite moves through it the way someone moves through an old house at night, recitation giving way without warning to symphonic light, a lyrical passage interrupted before it can settle, tension gathering, releasing, gathering again. It asks of the listener something like the patience Dolce Acqua once asked of a very different generation, back when sitting still with a record was still the ordinary way to spend an evening.- Io Clochard, I am a vagrant, the first human face the record offers once the suite's abstractions have passed, a song that studies a life lived entirely on the pavement with curiosity rather than judgment, the band's old melodic instinct returning gently instead of triumphantly.- Il Riposo del Pirata, the pirate's rest, an old adventurer finally still, the swagger gone out of him along with the urgency, the music settling exactly where its title promises, closer to elegy than to sea shanty.- Della Strada il Ritorno, the road's return, giving something back for once, a shorter piece answering the wandering of what came before with something like arrival, though never quite a homecoming.- Parole nel Vento, words in the wind, the close, scattering rather than gathering, the album ending not on a statement but on something nearer a shrug, which after everything before it feels like the most honest way to stop.Sesta Strada Lungo il Tempo does not try to be Dolce Acqua again, and it certainly does not try to repeat the accident of Jesahel. It knows, the way only musicians in their seventies can know, that the years do not grant a second youth, only a longer memory.What it offers instead is the sound of people who never really left the road, telling us, patiently, unhurriedly, what fifty five years of walking it has taught them. Anyone hoping for the old jolt of surprise will have to look elsewhere.Anyone willing to slow to the record's own pace will find a genuinely moving late chapter, faithful to everything the name Delirium has meant, from a bus borrowed for one unforgettable February evening to a Ligurian light that, exactly as Montale found, keeps its secrets simply by continuing. Highly recommended. My rating: 4,5/5
items._genre: Italian progressive rock / symphonic prog / classic prog
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由意大利老牌乐队Delirium重组后发行，延续了乐队自1970年代以来的意大利进步摇滚传统，乐评着重讲述了乐队从热那亚出发的历史脉络，包括创始人Ivano Fossati的离去、Martin Grice在1974年加入并塑造乐队声音的过程。乐评用文学性的笔触回顾了乐队跨越五十四年的演变，涉及Canto di Osanna、Jesahel等经典作品的背景。专辑延续了键盘与管乐主导的编曲风格，节奏更趋缓慢，试图表现时间与道路的意象。然而整体风格仍属传统意大利进步摇滚范畴，以人声和器乐旋律为主，缺乏前卫实验、爵士即兴、电子元素或世界音乐融合的明显特征，文章结尾截断也使音乐细节描述不够完整。

items.body: Elizabeth Cotten wrote “Freight Train” as a child, around eleven or twelve, growing up near Chapel Hill, North Carolina. Left-handed, with no one around to tell her otherwise, she strung a guitar for a right-handed player and simply flipped it upside down, picking the bass lines with her fingers and the melody with her thumb: a reversed technique that later got its own name, Cotten picking. Rhiannon Giddens, who grew up in Greensboro, a few hours from where Cotten did, has recorded her own version of the song for Hope Is the Thing with Feathers, her upcoming album out September 18 on Nonesuch Records. The take strips down to just her voice and Dirk Powell‘s acoustic guitar, matching the bareness of Cotten’s own 1958 recording. Cotten grew up next to freight trains and said she used to watch them go by; the lyrics ask, plainly, to keep hearing that same sound after she’s dead, calling out to be buried close enough to hear “old Number Nine” roll past. The album itself was recorded live at The Cypress House in Breaux Bridge, Louisiana, with few overdubs. Giddens kept the sound of the room in the mix: talk between takes, feet on the floor. Stream “Freight Train” HERE, and pre-order Hope Is the Thing with Feathers following THIS LINK The post Daily Discovery: Rhiannon Giddens – Freight Train appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._cn_summary: Rhiannon Giddens 在新专辑中翻唱了 Elizabeth Cotten 经典作品《Freight Train》，以人声与原声吉他的极简编制重现了 Cotten 1958 年录音的朴素质感。录制于路易斯安那州 Breaux Bridge 的 Cypress House，采用现场录音方式，保留了房间的自然声响如脚步声与段落间的交谈声。专辑标题《Hope Is the Thing with Feathers》取自 Emily Dickinson 诗作，由 Nonesuch Records 于 9 月 18 日发行。整张专辑强调原声根源音乐的传统与亲密度，Giddens 与 Dirk Powell 的演绎注重对原始材料的尊重而非风格扩展，内容更接近新闻发布而非深度乐评。

items.body: She Past Away are keeping the Mizantrop Tour on the road. The Turkish darkwave duo return to European stages on 23 September 2026 for a run that carries through to Christmas, and three Spanish shows have now been added for February 2027. The tour supports Mizantrop, the band’s fourth studio album, released on 11 February 2026 through Fabrika Records in Europe and Metropolis Records in North America. Mizantrop by She Past Away The autumn leg opens in Dublin and moves through the United Kingdom, Sweden, Norway, Poland, Germany, the Czech Republic, Belgium and the Netherlands. Two December shows close the year, at the Darkstorm Festival in Chemnitz on 25 December and at Lido in Berlin on 26 December. The newest additions are three Spanish dates in February 2027, presented by Fantaxtiks Events: Sala El Tren in Granada on 18 February, Sala Copérnico in Madrid on 19 February and Salamandra in L’Hospitalet de Llobregat, Barcelona, on 20 February. Tickets start at 28 euro and the shows are 16 and over. Three further 2027 dates follow later in the year, in Hannover, Vienna and Leipzig. She Past Away tour dates 23.09.2026 – Dublin, IE – Button Factory 25.09.2026 – Manchester, UK – Gorilla 26.09.2026 – Bristol, UK – Strange Brew 27.09.2026 – London, UK – EartH 23.10.2026 – Malmö, SE – Inkonst 24.10.2026 – Göteborg, SE – Musikens Hus 25.10.2026 – Oslo, NO – John Dee 28.10.2026 – Gdańsk, PL – Drizzly Grizzly 29.10.2026 – Warszawa, PL – Proxima 30.10.2026 – Poznań, PL – 2Progi 31.10.2026 – Kraków, PL – Kwadrat 03.11.2026 – Bielefeld, DE – Forum 04.11.2026 – Bremen, DE – Lagerhaus 05.11.2026 – Jena, DE – F-Haus 06.11.2026 – Kaiserslautern, DE – Kammgarn 07.11.2026 – München, DE – Katzenclub Festival 13.11.2026 – Prague, CZ – Futurum 14.11.2026 – Dresden, DE – Cold Hearted Festival 26.11.2026 – Sint-Niklaas, BE – De Casino 27.11.2026 – Heerlen, NL – Nieuwe Nor 28.11.2026 – Reutlingen, DE – franz.K 29.11.2026 – Haarlem, NL – Patronaat 25.12.2026 – Chemnitz, DE – Darkstorm Festival 26.12.2026 – Berlin, DE – Lido 18.02.2027 – Granada, ES – Sala El Tren 19.02.2027 – Madrid, ES – Sala Copérnico 20.02.2027 – Barcelona, ES – Salamandra 22.04.2027 – Hannover, DE – MusikZentrum 29.10.2027 – Wien, AT – Szene 06.11.2027 – Leipzig, DE – Täubchenthal A Glasgow show at Stereo on 24 September, listed on earlier versions of the itinerary, no longer appears on the band’s own tour page. About She Past Away She Past Away formed in Bursa, Turkey, in 2006, around Volkan Caner on vocals and guitar and İdris Akbulut on bass. The pair sang in Turkish from the start and built their sound on chorused guitar, drum machine and low, declarative vocals. Akbulut left in 2015 and producer Doruk Öztürkcan, who had been working with the band on keyboards and drum machine, became the second permanent member. The duo has operated in that form since. The EP “Kasvetli Kutlama” appeared in 2010 on the Turkish label Remoov. The debut album “Belirdi Gece” followed in 2012, first digitally and on CDr, then on vinyl through the Athens label Fabrika Records in 2013. “Narin Yalnızlık” arrived in 2015, again through Fabrika, and “Disko Anksiyete” in May 2019. Metropolis Records has handled North American editions of the catalogue since 2018, reissuing the first two albums that year and releasing “Disko Anksiyete” the following year. Between albums the duo issued the live record “Part Time Punks Session” in 2020 and the covers album “X” the same year, the 2021 single “Excess” with Perturbator, and the standalone single “İnziva” in September 2024. That track later became part of “Mizantrop”, the seven-song album released on 11 February 2026 with lyrics by Caner, composition and arrangement by Caner and Kerim Doruk Öztürkcan, and mixing, mastering and Dolby Atmos work by Erdinç Kaya. Physical editions followed through Fabrika on CD, vinyl and cassette, and through Metropolis in the United States in May 2026. The Mizantrop Tour has been running since spring 2026, taking in Istanbul, a North American leg, Wave-Gotik-Treffen in Leipzig and summer festival dates in Greece and Finland before the autumn run now under way.

items.body: (By our Norwegian correspondent Jan Ronald Stange / Apollon press release) Sometimes you’ll get a need to wind down a bit, let your mind drift off in solemn music instead of hard beating EBM rhythms. For that purpose the guitar- and synthdriven album “Change” released today by the Norwegian multi-instrumentalist Dan Heide would be a good fit. “Change” is the first solo album from Tønsberg’s Dan Heide, known for his guitar work in bands like Ljungblut, Zeromancer, X-Pleasure and many more. The album collects his previous one-off singles, spanning works all the way back from 2019, including the two new tracks “Change” and “I Byen et Sted”. Apollon Records issued it on 28 August 2026. The album is on Spotify, Tidal, YouTube Music, Deezer, Apple Music, Amazon Music, Bandcamp and Beatport, and is also available as a limited edition LP: 180g splatter vinyl with a 4-page booklet, limited to 200 copies. Bandcamp gives the vinyl a ship date of 28 September 2026; Apollon Records lists no date on its own product page. Dan Heide (Photo: Stine Heimsvik) The philosophy and thoughts behind the album Heide sets out the album’s scope and its division of production work: Dan Heide: “”Change” is a ten-track album, featuring nine original songs written by me and one song by Bob Dylan. I produced eight of the album’s tracks, while two were produced by Terje Johannesen. Musically, “Change” is a genre-defying album that reflects the breadth of my own musical taste, bringing together different genres, textures and forms of musical expression. The need to release a solo album is something that has gradually evolved over time. Having worked across numerous bands and projects, my solo project has become a small creative playground – a space where anything is possible, where I can follow my own inspiration freely and without commercial considerations. At the heart of “Change” is a common thread exploring change and the emotions that surround it. The songs approach the theme from different perspectives, touching on personal reflections, shifting moods and the many emotional states we can find ourselves in. “Change” is, for the most part, a quiet and understated record. Yet beneath its calm surface lies a subtle, but powerful expression, allowing the music, the atmosphere and the emotions to unfold at their own pace. It’s a deeply personal album: an honest reflection of my musical curiosity, my influences and my desire to create freely, without boundaries.” Dan Heide ‘Change’: the ten tracks “Are You All Right?” “Change” “I Byen et Sted” “Close to Me” “Sometimes” “The Night Sky” “Dine Øyne” “The Times They Are A-Changin'” “Every Now and Then” “In God’s Country” The Bob Dylan song Heide refers to is “The Times They Are A-Changin'”, recorded with Kjell Arne Strøm-Olsen. Six of the other nine appeared first as one-off singles: “Sometimes” in October 2019, “In God’s Country” in September 2020, “Close to Me” in May 2023, “Are You All Right?” in October 2024, “Every Now and Then” in January 2025 and “The Night Sky” in April 2025. “In God’s Country” and “Sometimes” were also paired on a 2021 7-inch for Apollon Records and Gymnocal Industries. The album leaves out three other singles from the same stretch, “Awkward Star” (2023), the “Ambient in C Major” EP (2023) and “This Old Feeling” (2024). Change by Dan Heide Listen to “Change” on Spotify | Tidal | YouTube Music | Deezer | Apple Music/iTunes | Amazon Music | Bandcamp | Beatport | Qobuz | Soundcloud, or buy the vinyl directly from Apollon Records. About Dan Heide Dan-André Heide Syversen, who records as Dan Heide, is a guitarist, multi-instrumentalist and producer from Tønsberg, Norway. He first appeared on record with X-Pleasure, playing guitar and singing on the band’s self-titled 2003 album alongside his brother Ruben Heide Syversen; the group returned in 2024 with “His Master’s Voice”, written by Heide and arranged by the band. He played guitar in Zeromancer from 2003 to 2018, and is credited on “Sinners International” (2009), “The Death of Romance” (2010) and “Bye-Bye Borderline” (2013). He also recorded a double album with Kim Ljung as Ljungblut, playing guitar on “Capitals” (2007) and appearing on the project’s releases since. Further credits include guitar on Red 7‘s “Silence Hotel” (2016) and a performing credit on Pigface‘s “6” (2009). His solo work began as a run of singles rather than albums, starting with “Sometimes” in 2019 and continuing at roughly one or two releases a year. Side-Line spoke to him in June 2025 around the single “Change”, in an interview about the single ‘Change’ in which he discussed the writing behind it. That single now opens the second slot on the album of the same name, his first full-length under his own name. Do also check his YouTube profile for more music and videos.

items.body: 2026.08.28 「建築家が聴いた音楽―建築家・土浦亀城の思考に響いた音」演奏会シリーズ 第3回「内面としてのロマン派：シューベルト」 建築家・土屋亀城（1897–1996）がどのような音楽を、どのような感覚で聴いていたのか。「建築家が聴いた音楽―建築家・土浦亀城の思考に響いた音」は、昭和初期の住宅建築を代表する名作・土浦亀城邸で、音楽作品を演奏し、対話によって思考を深める、全6回の対話型演奏会シリーズ。 9月16日（水）にひらかれるシリーズ第3回は、「内面としてのロマン派：シューベルト」。今ここでシューベルトを聴く企図を、本演奏会シリーズで総合監修・ナビゲーターを務める、音楽学者の久保田慶一先生に伺いました。 ONTOMO編集部 東京・神楽坂にある音楽之友社を拠点に、Webマガジン「ONTOMO」の企画・取材・編集をしています。「音楽っていいなぁ、を毎日に。」を掲げ、やさしく・ふかく・おもしろ... 詳しく見る 建築と音楽を対話で紐解く深い体験 ——「建築家が聴いた音楽―建築家・土浦亀城の思考に響いた音」はどのような演奏会シリーズでしょうか。 久保田 今回の演奏会シリーズのコンセプトは、建築と音楽の接点として、6つの視点から音楽を聴くことにあります。構造、くつろぎ、内面、色彩、均整、素材という視点です。 建築には構造が必要ですが、音楽には楽器、音階、音楽のそれぞれの構造があります。自宅で人々はくつろぎ、音楽を聴いてもくつろぎます。また物思いにふけって自分の内面を見つめるには、静かな空間が必要です。内装の色、全体の均整、素材がそこに住むわれわれの感性を刺激し、また同時に、やすらぎを与えます。 建築と音楽のそれぞれが作る空間を楽しむことが、今回のシリーズの目的です。建物のなかに入って「ここに住んでみたい」、「ここで音楽を聴いてみたい」という願いを叶えてくれる演奏会です。 ©土浦亀城アーカイブズ 土浦亀城邸 東京都指定有形文化財（建造物） 建築家・土浦亀城が米国でフランク・ロイド・ライトに学び、帰国後1935年に竣工した自邸。昭和10年代にあって、現代にも通じるような「健康的な楽しい暮らし」をアイデアで実現し、プライバシーのある空間も備えつつ、文化的な仲間との豊かな時間の共有も叶えた。自然光に満ちた、日本のモダニズム木造住宅を代表する名作。また土浦亀城は、バッハから20世紀音楽に至る幅広いジャンルを好み、電蓄で音楽を聴くことがこの住宅で過ごす愉しみのひとつだった。工夫にあふれた建築は見どころが多く、今回のシューベルト・プログラムと相高めあう空間に演奏会への期待が高まる。 【所在地】東京都港区南青山2-5-13 【原設計】土浦亀城・土浦信子 （1935年 品川区上大崎） 【復原・移築設計】 安田アトリエ 【実測調査・実測図面・模型制作】 東京工業大学安田幸一研究室（当時） ——シリーズ第3回「内面としてのロマン派：シューベルト」では、歌曲にも言葉があり、対話にも言葉が生まれますね。言葉の存在、人間の声が持つ魔法をダイレクトに感じられるのではないかと興味深いです。プログラムの意図や聴きどころをお聞かせください。 久保田 今回演奏される歌曲の歌詞はすべてドイツ語です。プログラムには原語の詩は掲載せずに、日本語訳だけにしてあります。 お話のなかで私が強調したいのは、声を楽器の音として聴いてくださいということです。意味を理解する必要はありません。ドイツ語の子音や母音の連続がつくる響きやリズムを、ラップを聴くように楽しんでもらえればいいと思います。ただしキーワードになる言葉の原語はお伝えして、いっしょに発音してもらうつもりです。例えば、小川を意味する「バッハBach」など。 また私のお話では、詩の内容に関連して、聴衆の方々に、ご自身の経験や記憶を辿っていただきます。今回は恋愛に関する歌曲が多いので、若い日のあるいは現在進行中の恋愛、あるいはそこまでいかなくても、子どもや孫への愛情などについて、私から質問をして、ご自身の内面を掘り下げていただきます。そのうえで、歌曲を聴くことで、その経験や記憶と音楽が「化学変化」を起こします。つまり、音楽を「わたくし事」として聴いてもらうのです。こうすることで、音楽を聴くという経験がより深くなっていきます。 例えば、東日本大震災の復興支援歌として知られた「花は咲く」がありますが、その歌を復興支援歌として聴くのと、亡くなられた祖父母の記憶を思いだして聴くのとでは、歌を聴いたときの印象が異なることは想像できますね。「わたくし事」として音楽を聴くということは、そういうことです。音楽はいかようにも聴いていいわけですね。 久保田慶一（音楽学者） 東京藝術大学大学院修士課程修了。音楽学博士（東京藝術大学大学院）。フライブルク大学、ハンブルク大学、ベルリン自由大学に留学。東京学芸大学教授、国立音楽大学教授・副学長、東京経済大学客員教授を経て、現在、日本大学大学院ならびに放送大学講師。専門は18世紀ドイツ音楽史。『バッハ』（音楽之友社、2021年）他、著書多数。「建築家が聴いた音楽―建築家・土浦亀城の思考に響いた音」では総合監修・ナビゲーターを務める。 ——今回演奏されるテノールの片野耕喜さん、フォルテピアノの小川加恵さんについて教えてください。 久保田 おふたりとも、私とは旧知であり教え子でもあります。彼らの演奏も何度も聴いています。 対話型演奏会を銘打ってはいますが、私と聴衆の方との会話はかなり限られています。そこで、演奏の合間に、私と演奏者が演奏する曲や楽器など、いろんな対話をします。これまで2回演奏会をしましたが、なかなか好評だったようです。 片野耕喜 （テノール） 小川加恵（フォルテピアノ） ——小川さんは貴重なフォルテピアノを演奏されるので、片野さんと小川さんと楽器が土浦亀城邸でどのように響くのか、楽しみです。シューベルトとフォルテピアノの時代・土浦亀城邸の時代をめぐる、時空を超えた体験となりそうですね。楽器の魅力についてもお聞かせください。 久保田 シューベルトは生前、同時代に同じ場所に住んでいたベートーヴェンとは異なり、大きな公的な会場で自作品を演奏したことがありません。「シューベルティアーデ」と呼ばれたサロンで演奏していました。フォルテピアノはそのような空間にぴったりの楽器です。シューベルトの音楽を理解するためには、当時響いた音や空間を経験することが欠くことはできないでしょう。 フォルテピアノ ルイ・ドゥルケンモデル（1790年頃） クリス・マーネ製作（1989年） 音域：FF~f3 （５オクターブ） ダンパー：膝ペダル モデレーター：手動式 message from 小川加恵 今回使用するのは、シューベルトが生まれた頃と同時代、1790年頃のウィーンのフォルテピアノをモデルとした楽器です。現代のピアノとは異なる、軽やかで透明感のある響きと、まるで言葉を語るような繊細な表情が魅力です。   今回はシューベルトの《君がここにいたことを》《ガニュメート》《鱒》、シューマンの《詩人の恋》より《君の目に見入ると》など、詩と音楽が深く結びついた歌曲をお楽しみいただきます。歌詞に描かれた情景や心の機微を、フォルテピアノがどのように「歌い、語る」のかにも耳を傾けていただければと思います。   先見性を持ちながらも、人の暮らしに寄り添う親密な空間として設計された土浦邸と、もともとサロンや家庭など身近な空間で楽しまれていたフォルテピアノ。その親和性から生まれる響きとともに、音楽を間近に感じていただける特別なひとときを私自身とても楽しみにしています。 ——ご来場のみなさまに、本演奏会をたのしむコツやメッセージをお願いします。 久保田 音楽の聴き方は人さまざまです。またこの曲にはこのような聴き方が「ベスト」であるということもありません。一般的な聴き方や傾向はあると思います。 演奏会では、演奏者が身体を通して発した音や音楽を聴き、そこから得られるイメージ、感情、情景を楽しんでもらえればといいと思います。「聴いてよかった」「また同じ曲を、同じ作曲家の、同じ演奏家の音楽を聴いてみたい」と思っていただけるのが、企画者としては「ベスト」です。 音楽は一定の空間の中で聴かれることを想定して作曲され、また演奏されます。空間に響く音の振動は、われわれの人間の皮膚をも振動させています。演奏者と聴衆の身体は、空間と音を介して、共鳴しているとも言えます。こうしたことを経験すること、またその良さを伝えていくことが、今後、音楽が多くの人に愛されていくためには必要であると思っています。 items._cn_summary: 本文介绍了一场在建筑师土浦龟城旧居举办的舒伯特歌曲演奏会，属于该系列对话型音乐会的第三回。演出由男高音与古钢琴（fortepiano）合作，曲目包括舒伯特及舒曼的德语艺术歌曲。文章通过音乐学者久保田庆一的访谈，强调以建筑与音乐对话的视角聆听，并提出将人声视为乐器音色、不依赖歌词理解、唤起个人记忆与情感来加深音乐体验的理念。演奏空间本身是昭和初期现代主义住宅，具有历史与文化氛围，古钢琴的音色也贴近舒伯特时代的沙龙风格。整体上，这是一场将建筑空间、历史乐器与经典曲目结合的音乐活动，但音乐本身属于传统古典浪漫派曲目，并非当代或实验性创作。

items._cn_summary: 本文是一篇日本古典音乐演出周报，整理并推荐了8月31日至9月6日期间在北海道、岩手、福岛、东京等多地举行的多场音乐会。内容涵盖弦乐四重奏、钢琴独奏、交响乐与协奏曲等常规古典形式，曲目以拉威尔、贝多芬、布鲁克纳、柴可夫斯基等作曲家为主，同时也包含武满彻、三善晃、史蒂夫·莱希等现代与极简主义作品。文章重点在于提供演出时间、地点、参演音乐家、门票信息等实用导览，并未对具体音乐演绎进行深入分析，属于资讯推荐而非乐评。整体以主流古典曲目为主，与实验、前卫等偏好关联较弱，仅少数当代作品具有一定契合度。

items.body: It's been a while since we've visited with one of my favorite "microscenes" - the French stoner and doom metal scene. Luckily, one of my favorite bands from that area of the world are back with a new album this year and have graciously afforded me the privilege of premiering a single from said album. I covered Pelegrin for the first time four years ago with another premiere and I've been waiting for more music since then. Happily, "Sun and Blood" does not disappoint with a trippy, occult-steeped video and, more importantly, a more muscular and present approach to Pelegrin's sound than before. Head on down below to take the journey!Pelegrin's previous music can be described as "airy", a certain thinness which worked very well with the expansive can of psychedelia they were going for. But here, the adjective would be "earthy" - the main riff is much more present in the mix, its tone thicker and heavier. The drums are punctual like falling stones, lending the track momentum and groove. Sprinkle in the same excellent vocals from the previous release, one scorching, desert-sun hot solo, and a few more touches here and there from excellent backing riffs and thick bass, and you've got yourself a treat. I also love the lighter guitars which open the track, setting the ground for the shimmering, stoner sound the band is so good for."Sun and Blood" comes to us from the upcoming The Curse of Nephtar, due to release on September 4th on the mighty Ripple Music. You can head on over here to pre-order it (and also check out that glorious art work in full).
items._genre: stoner metal / doom metal / psychedelic rock
items._cn_summary: 法国石人/厄运金属乐队Pelegrin新单曲《Sun and Blood》延续其迷幻风格，但整体取向更为厚重扎实。主音riff在混音中更突出，音色更浓重，鼓点如落石般精准，带来明显推进感和律动。人声保持水准，吉他独奏带有沙漠烈日般的灼热感，低音与伴奏riff增添层次。乐曲以轻快吉他开场，逐步引入标志性的闪耀石人音色。该曲出自即将发行的专辑《The Curse of Nephtar》，由Ripple Music厂牌推出。作品整体属于类型内的常规表达，缺乏实验性或跨领域融合元素，与偏好前卫、爵士、电子等方向的口味距离较远。

items.body: 「音楽」に深いこだわりを持つ飲食店を紹介するこのコーナー。今回は富士見ヶ丘（東京都杉並区）にあるパン屋『ヨシダベーカリー』を訪問。ここは通常営業時からレコードで音楽が流れており、週に一日程度、夕方からレコードバーに変身するユニークなお店でもあります。真空管アンプやヴィンテージ・スピーカーが置かれ、パン好きはもちろん音楽好きにとってもワクワクする空間でした。 音楽好きの店主が営むベーカリー 京王井の頭線 富士見ヶ丘駅 南口から徒歩約1分。マンション1Fにお店が連なる一画にある、白を基調としたおしゃれな外観の『ヨシダベーカリー』。国産小麦を使った風味豊かなパンをはじめ、サンドイッチやタルトなども豊富に揃う人気のお店。 「美味しいパン屋さん」としてさまざまなメディアで取り上げられており、パン好きには知られた存在だ。その証拠に、平日の昼間でもひっきりなしに常連客がやってくる。 店内に足を踏み入れると、香ばしい小麦の香りと共に、見た目にも美しいパンが勢揃い。何を買おうかワクワクして選んでいると、ふと「ん？ このお店音良いな」と音楽好きなら気づくはずだ。 ショーケースのパン越しに視点をずらすと、ターンテーブルの上でレコードが回っている。「BGMをレコードで流しているパン屋？」という不思議な組み合わせに驚いていると、真空管アンプやヴィンテージ・スピーカーなども次々と発見。「どういうこと？」と疑問が浮かんでくる。 「音楽好きなので、やっぱりいい音で聴きたいなということで。オーディオに関しては、子どもの頃から好きだったんです」。そう語るのは、店主の吉田 稔さん。 東京・葛飾区で1976年に生まれた吉田さんは、小学生のときに通っていたそろばん塾の先生がスピーカーを自作するタイプだった。それを譲り受けて以来、オーディオに興味を持つようになったという。 先生の影響でビートルズなども聴いていたが、当時流行っていたBOØWYやCOMPLEXなども聴いていたとか。その後、10代後半になるとHMV渋谷やZESTに行き始め、渋谷系をはじめとする90年代カルチャーに触れるようになる。そこから、好きなアーティストが影響を受けた音楽を探したりと、レコードを掘るようになった。 「最初はトラットリア（Trattoria Records）とかクルーエル（Crue-L Records）とか。そこからフリーソウルを聴いたり、その延長でジャズやブラジルを聴いたり、いろいろな音楽を聴くようになったんです」 高校を卒業して社会経験を積むなか、次第に一つのことを追求していきたいと思うようになったという。そんな折、夫婦で営むパン屋が近所にでき、店主と話しているうちにやりたいことが見えてきた。 「パン屋をやりながら、好きな音楽を聴けたらいいなというイメージができたんです」 転機は、フルオート再生のレコードプレイヤー その後、6年ほどパンづくりの修行をおこない2012年に独立。現在の場所で『ヨシダベーカリー』をオープンする。しかし、当初からレコードをかけていたわけではなかった。 「常に粉まみれなので、レコード盤を頻繁にひっくり返すことができないんです。なので、最初はCDをiTunesに落として聴いていたんですけど、あるときリピート機能のあるフルオート再生のレコードプレイヤーを見つけて。これなら使えると思ったんです」 販売スタッフに操作をお願いするのは難しいため、現在も通常営業時は片面がリピート再生されていることが多い。ひと段落ついたとき、手を洗って盤を交換するのが日常だ。 「当初は、クワイエットミュージックとか、アルゼンチンのネオ・フォルクローレとかポストクラシカルを流していて。レコードプレイヤーを導入してからは、クラシックにのめり込んでいくんです。チェロの無伴奏ものなど、いろいろな作曲家のものを集めてみたり。協奏曲とかも気になるものは集めていきました。クラシックは安いからいっぱい買えるんですよ（笑）」 しかし最近は、広範囲のアンビエントや現代的なワールドミュージックなど、新譜が中心になってきている。それに合わせ、ヴィンテージのスピーカーのみならず、最新のスピーカーも導入。音楽や気分に合わせて切り替えながら、パンづくりに勤しんでいる。 どんな曲が流れているのか、どんなパンが売られているのかは、Instagramをチェックするとより理解できるだろう。 現在の機材は、レコードプレイヤーがテクニクスのSL-1300MK2。フルオート機能付きのものでは、当時もっとも性能が良いとされていた名品だ。アンプは、近所に住むセミプロのビルダーさんによる、300Bの真空管を使ったもの。所有していた2A3の真空管アンプを修理するタイミングで借りたものだという。 店内のスピーカーは、60年代のテレフンケン（ドイツ）RB-70と、50年代のレーベ・オプタ（ドイツ）のユニットをヴィンテージジョインがマウントしたもの。さらに、超薄板ガラスがコーン部分に使われている、マークオーディオのNC5H_UTAG。作業場のスピーカーはマークオーディオのCESTI MBだ。 さらに、ブレーカースイッチをオーディオ用のものに変更し、光城精工のパワーコンディショナー（≒クリーン電源）、マークオーディオのリニア電源を使うなど、良い音を支える環境にも抜かりがない。 「理想のサウンドというのはとくにないんです。音楽ジャンルや曲がつくられた年代に合わせて、まろやか系から解像度の高いものまで、気分で切り替えながら楽しんでいます。でも、自分も職人なので、クラフト系の機器に共感することが多いかもしれない」 週に一日程度、レコードバーとしてもオープン この連載は、「音楽」に深いこだわりを持つ飲食店を紹介することがコンセプト。このままでは飲食店ではなく、販売店だというツッコミが入りそうだ。しかし、『ヨシダベーカリー』は2026年3月より、週に一日程度レコードバーとしてオープンするようになっている。 「このところレコードを買いすぎているので、もっと有効活用しなくてはという思いもあって。パン屋のB面的な感じで、思いつきで始めたんです。これまでも、パンのオーブンで珈琲を焙煎したり、クレープ屋さんを不定期でやったり、自家製麺をつくったり、餃子をつくったり、この設備と自分の技術でできることをいろいろやっているんです」 レコードバーとして営業する際は、カウンター上の什器を撤去してオールスタンディングのバーに変更。照明は小さな電球とキャンドルのみ。 お酒はクラフトビールをはじめ、コニャックやカルバドスなど珍しいブランデーを多く揃えている。また、パンやタコスなどフィンガーフードとして食べられるおつまみも用意される。 「接客は得意ではないんですけど、自分の好きな音楽をかけて共感してくれたり、いろいろな話をしてコミュニケーションできるのは楽しいですね。ルーティンワークにならないよう、今後もいろいろやりながら、本業のパンをブラッシュアップでさせていきたいと思っています」 取材・文／富山英三郎 撮影／高瀬竜弥 ・店舗名 ヨシダベーカリー ・住所 東京都杉並区久我山2-23-29 ハイネス富士見ヶ丘 1F ・営業時間 11:00〜19:00（パン屋営業）、18:30〜23:30（レコードバー営業） ・定休日 水曜・日曜 （レコードバーは定休日に営業することが多い。Instagramを要確認） 投稿 【東京・富士見ヶ丘 ヨシダベーカリー】レコードバーにも変身する美味しいベーカリー は ARBAN に最初に表示されました。
items._cn_summary: 本文并非乐评，而是一篇关于东京富士见之丘一家兼营唱片酒吧的面包店《吉田面包店》的店铺介绍。文章围绕店主吉田稔先生的音乐爱好展开：他自幼接触音响，经历了从Beatles、BOØWY到90年代涩谷系、Trattoria厂牌系音乐和Free Soul的听音历程。店铺通常营业时播放唱片，内容涵盖阿尔ゼンチン新民谣、后古典、古典无伴奏、大提琴协奏曲等，近期转向广范围氛围音乐和现代世界音乐。器材方面使用Technics SL-1300MK2唱盘、300B真空管放大器、Telefunken和JBL等古董音箱，并搭配最新音箱切换使用。2026年3月起每周开放一日作为唱片酒吧。全文虽展现了店主对音乐与面包结合的生活理念，但内容偏向店铺探访报道，缺乏对音乐本身的深度评论与分析。

items._cn_summary: 牙买加雷鬼老将卡普尔顿时隔十五年发表的新作，由利特尔·莱昂·声音厂牌发行。整张专辑在激进与沉稳之间寻找平衡：机枪式咆哮说唱搭配军事化律动，直指巴比伦的压迫与不公；同时又以包容的歌唱姿态引导听众追求精神层面的升华。白眉之作是与达米安与史蒂芬兄弟合作的一首单曲，将上述两种气质融为一体，并巧妙引用了丹尼斯·布朗的经典旋律作为致敬。从风格定位来看，这张专辑属于典型的牙买加舞蹈厅与根源雷鬼范畴，强调社会批判意识与拉斯特法里精神信仰的传达，对偏好实验、前卫、爵士或电子等领域的听众而言，契合度较为有限。

items.body:
Since everyone else has written something about the centennials of Miles Davis and John Coltrane, why not join the parade? It is a good opportunity to look at the timeline of bassists the legendary trumpeter and saxophonist used. Born just under four months apart, the pair worked together under the elder Davis’ name periodically between Fall 1955 and Spring 1957 before a more steady affiliation in 1958-1960.

It is in that latter period that this analysis will begin, as it gives a convenient bit of serendipity: the fact that two of the their most famed albums were made in that period, Davis’ Kind Blue (March 2nd and April 22nd, 1959 for Columbia) and Coltrane’s Giant Steps (May 4th–5th and December 2nd, 1959). And the analysis will end with Coltrane’s death in 1967, which came during the tenure of Davis’ “second great quintet” and before his groups swelled and electrified during his fusion period.

As such, we begin with the same man, the bassist on both those albums: Paul Chambers. He had taken up the bass a decade earlier in his adopted home of Detroit (where he was a student at the seminal Cass Technical High School ... more on that later). He arrived in New York in 1954 at 19. By the time of Kind of Blue and Giant Steps, he had been on over 100 sessions from dozens of leaders, with multiple dates under Davis (with whom he had started working in late 1955) and Coltrane (who had used him for several albums in 1957-58 as well as both fellow sideman for many others and Chambers also hiring Coltrane for his own sessions). In addition to the five albums he led, Chambers played on sessions for Benny Golson, Curtis Fuller, J.J. Johnson, Lee Morgan, Red Garland, Sonny Clark, and Sonny Rollins.

The collaboration between Davis and Chambers was remarkably fruitful before and after Kind of Blue and solidified a part of Davis’ music that had previously seen widely differing players like Tommy Potter, Oscar Pettiford, Al McKibbon, and Percy Heath. The rest of 1959 saw multiple engagements around the country and closed with recordings that would be part of another monumental record, Sketches of Spain, that paired Davis’ group with the Gil Evans Orchestra. 1960 continued that momentum with more Sketches of Spain recording and almost non-stop touring, including two stretches in Europe, from Spring onward. 1961 and 1962 had more of the same activity, the documents being Someday My Prince Will Come and Quiet Nights. Then, quite suddenly, Chambers left Davis’ group in early February 1963.

It should be stated that Chambers did not restrict his activities solely to Davis, recording over four dozen albums during the period with, among many others, Jackie McLean, Wynton Kelly, Benny Golson, Hank Mobley, and Curtis Fuller. And after leaving Davis, he worked steadily with an array of leaders through the end of 1968, sadly passing away from tuberculosis caused and/or aggravated by drug abuse at only 33.

Stepping right into the Davis group was another Cass Technical High School alumnus: Ron Carter. Nearly 26, Carter was already prophesying his prolific career, participating in over three dozen albums since 1960, with the likes of Charli Persip, Yusef Lateef, Eric Dolphy, Don Ellis, Coleman Hawkins, Cecil Payne, Jaki Byard, Wes Montgomery, Bobby Timmons, Tadd Dameron, Dizzy Reece, Ken McIntyre, Milt Jackson, Benny Golson and others, plus waxing his leader debut, Where?, for Prestige subsidiary New Jazz in 1961.

It was Carter’s arrival that heralded Davis’ soon-to-be seminal band, though it took until Fall 1964 for its personnel to solidify. With Carter, Davis recorded Seven Steps To Heaven and played the Antibes festival in 1963. What is interesting though is while the “second great quintet” is thought of as a monolith, the bass chair had some upheaval/fluidity, depending on how you look at it. Gary Peacock – already a veteran and likely the only person to work for both Bud Shank and Albert Ayler – took the chair for nearly six weeks in the spring of 1964, Carter returning thereafter through the end of the year. 1965 began auspiciously with the January recording of E.S.P. but then things derailed with a convalescing Davis unable to play. And when he could, in November and December, Carter, a hot commodity, was absent, spelled by Peacock once more, then Reggie Workman, who had come up around the same time as Carter and had already come and gone in the groups of Coltrane. In 1966, Carter would return to the group but only partially, participating in East Coast performances, shows elsewhere having either Richard Davis, Carter’s only real equal in terms of fecundity, or in the Peacock mold of eclecticism, Eddie Gomez, returning permanently in October, just before the album Miles Smiles. 1967 was similar: Carter was on board when not busy elsewhere, Gomez on call, then Albert Stinson for one show (a little over two years before his passing – see Bass Tragedies column in Issue 94) and then another veteran, Buster Williams, for a tour (and playing on one track of the 1981-released compilation album Directions). Carter would fill a fixed point for all of 1967, including the albums Sorcerer and Nefertiti and would continue with Davis through the middle of 1968.

Like Chambers or perhaps even more so, Carter was also on the greater jazz scene during his tenure with Davis. He recorded on sessions led by his fellow Davis bandmates but also by everyone from Bobby Timmons, Charles Lloyd, Donald Byrd and Bobby Hutcherson to Jimmy Smith, Shirley Scott, Eddie Harris, and Stanley Turrentine, to name only a handful. He has, of course, gone on to be likely the most recorded bassist in jazz history.

Paul Chambers’ time under Coltrane was shorter and more intermittent. After Giant Steps he was part of, along with the rest of Davis’ period band, November 1959 recordings that would partly comprise Coltrane Jazz and be brought back 18 months later as one of three individual bassists taking part in the Africa/Brass recordings (though his contribution was only heard on the 1995 complete sessions version).

Also in 1959 was a Birdland engagement for Coltrane where either Ahmed Abdul-Malik or George Tucker, both established and close in age to Coltrane, were on bass.

In 1960 Coltrane hired the slightly younger Steve Davis in what seems to be his first professional engagement. Davis stayed in the band through the end of the year for all its live dates and played on music recorded in October and released piecemeal on My Favorite Things, Coltrane Jazz, Coltrane Plays the Blues, and Coltrane’s Sound. Though Davis lived until 1987, his credits after Coltrane were slight: the Mangione Brothers, Dave Burns, McCoy Tyner, Kenny Dorham, James Moody, Freddie McCoy, and Eddie Jefferson, all made in the ‘60s. One deviation in the year came via Coltrane’s shared date with Don Cherry, The Avant-Garde, where bass was handled by either Charlie Haden or Percy Heath.

1961 was a year in flux, bassist-wise, for Coltrane. He introduced a concept to which he would return later in the decade by using two bassists for an engagement at Chicago’s Sutherland Lounge in March: Raphael Don Garrett and Workman, the former, about six years younger, working with Roland Kirk, Paul Serrano, and Eddie Harris, the latter 11 years younger, sideman for Gigi Gryce, Donald Byrd, Duke Jordan, Richard Williams, and Dave Pike.

Workman would be part of the aforementioned Africa/Brass, as would, separately, another bassist, Art Davis, already with credits under Max Roach, Lee Morgan, Booker Little, Hal Mooney, Ernestine Anderson, Dizzy Gillespie, Leo Wright, Clifford Jordan/Sonny Red, Abbey Lincoln, and Booker Little. But in May they were together for Ole Coltrane and nearly a month at the Village Vanguard in August. Workman would become the fixed bassist for Coltrane through the end of the year for concerts, including a European tour, and a small portion of the Ballads album from the end of the year. An exception was Workman either alternating or alongside Jimmy Garrison for a November stint at the Village Vanguard.

If not for a family health crisis forcing Workman to leave the group at the end of 1961 and return to his native Philadelphia, he likely would have stayed with the band and jazz history been quite different. It should be said that Workman hardly is a footnote, becoming one of the most revered players of his generation. But it was Garrison who became the anchor. Born between Garrett and Workman, prior to joining Coltrane he had worked with Philly Joe Jones, Curtis Fuller, Kenny Dorham, Jackie McLean, JR Montrose, Walter Bishop, Jr., Ornette Coleman, Bill Barron, and Ted Curson.

Unlike Carter and Davis, once Garrison was on board, he stayed there. That was mostly to do with Coltrane’s packed schedule of touring and albums and that, unlike Davis, he was healthy and non-combustible. From 1962-1964, Garrison was omnipresent, including the bulk of Ballads, Duke Ellington & John Coltrane (where he split duties with Ellington’s period bassist Aaron Bell), 2018 discovery Both Directions At Once, John Coltrane And Johnny Hartman, Impressions, Crescent, another new millennium unearthed gem in Blue World, and closing out the year with Coltrane’s magnum opus A Love Supreme (which added Art Davis for a second day of recording, released as a second disc to the album’s deluxe edition in 2002).

In 1965 Garrison was still the main man but occasionally Davis would be alongside him: partially on The John Coltrane Quartet Plays in February and fully for June’s Ascension. Otherwise, Garrison was the sole bassist for performances and most of the other albums: Transition, Sun Ship, and Meditations. The exceptions without Davis were overdubs of Haden for the posthumously released Infinity and Garrett returning to play both bass and clarinet for Live In Seattle (as well as the 2021 archival release A Love Supreme: Live In Seattle), Om, and part of Kulu Se Mama.

1966 was even more Garrison-centric, with the only documented work including a second bassist shows in November and December with Lionel “Sonny” Johnson, the brother of Dewey Johnson, who had played on Ascension. The last year of Coltrane’s life, Garrison was there as well, with one notable absence: the Coltrane/Rashied Ali duet Interstellar Space.

Unlike Chambers or Carter, Garrison was kept so busy during his time with Coltrane that his outside discography at the time is meager, though it does include his sole leader date, Illumination! with the Elvin Jones/Jimmy Garrison Sextet. Otherwise it was sessions with Lorez Alexandria, Coltrane bandmate McCoy Tyner, Sonny Rollins, Bill Dixon, and Robert F. Pozar.

After Coltrane’s death, Garrison kept working but his documentation slowed, his two Blue Note dates with the Jones trio rounded out by Joe Farrell being the most enduring. There were also dates with Rolf and Joachim Kuhn, Clifford Thornton and Nathan Davis, and regular work with Alice Coltrane and Archie Shepp. His final recording came in early 1975 with Beaver Harris and Dave Burrell’s 360 Degree Music Experience. Garrison died of lung cancer in 1976 at 42.

items._cn_summary: 本文以Miles Davis和John Coltrane百年诞辰为契机，梳理两人合作期间所用的贝斯手脉络。从Paul Chambers在Kind of Blue和Giant Steps的根基地位，到他广泛的sideman经历和早逝，再到接替者来自同一底特律Cass Technical高中的渊源。文章本质是爵士史的人物关系考据，重在纪实性的时间线与唱片列表梳理，缺乏对音乐本身的听觉分析或批评性观点。对于关注实验、前卫或即兴深水区的读者而言，此类传统主流爵士叙事的信息密度有限。
